Two covers required more handling, but kept two different decisions readable.

court_rain_gust_interrupt.speaker: narrator
court_rain_gust_interrupt.text: A gust drove rain across the arch and sent the route attendant's loose cord striking the wall. The Heron lowered its body and called attention to the changing local wind. The attendant paused passage until the covered footing was checked. Lin Yue waited inside the marked recess rather than trying to finish the visit by slipping past him. Their samples were sealed; no urgent observation required another body on the path. Luo Shan wrote the pause as a current access action. It did not retroactively prove what conditions had been present during the earlier accident.

court_rain_bulletin_approach.speaker: narrator
court_rain_bulletin_approach.text: When passage resumed, they returned by the covered route and left the protected arch behind. Day one's work had produced more distinctions than accusations. The clock bands, material custody lines, and equipment list would all need explanation before the common hearing. The next morning, Luo Shan would compare the offered weather log with the court's public bulletins. Lin Yue looked at the white ribbon on the outer gate as they passed. It remained closed, a present boundary that did useful work without claiming to answer every question about an earlier day.

court_rain_bulletin_entry.speaker: narrator
court_rain_bulletin_entry.text: On Day two, Luo Shan unrolled two public weather bulletins on the witness-room table. The paper smelled faintly of paste and damp wood. Their numbered publication entries established an earlier notice and a later revision, while the printed hour labels came from different named clocks. Lin Yue placed the current clock bands beside them without applying those bands backward. The Heron settled on a wide sill and asked to see the offered log copy before its words were discussed. An authorized clerk brought the source comparison sheet, keeping the unrelated nesting pages covered.

court_rain_earlier_bulletin.speaker: narrator
court_rain_earlier_bulletin.text: The earlier notice described rising cloud and possible rain along exposed edges on the disputed day. It also said that a full outer observation had not been completed. A copied summary elsewhere had dropped that last sentence. Luo Shan read the complete public notice aloud, including its limits. The omission did not establish why the summary was shortened. It did explain why a reader might think the forecast rested on a view no one had offered. Lin Yue asked the clerk to attach the complete notice rather than merely correcting a sentence inside the investigator's own argument.

court_rain_revised_bulletin.speaker: narrator
court_rain_revised_bulletin.text: The later revision distinguished reported rain at the inner rail from conditions that remained unobserved at the outer spur. Its publication number came after the earlier notice in the register. That sequence did not place the revision precisely before or after the sling slip, because the relevant time sources still lacked a supported alignment. Shen Qing drew two arrows: one for known publication order, one ending in an open interval beside the accident report. The separate arrows kept a real documentary sequence from acquiring an exact relationship the pages could not establish.

court_rain_publication_source.speaker: narrator
court_rain_publication_source.text: The bulletin clerk showed the register's consecutive spaces and the receipt for the later sheet. Its copy had been handed to a runner after the register entry, with the runner's acknowledgment preserved beneath it. Lin Yue asked whether that proved when every person below first read the notice. It did not. Some copies reached shops later, and one runner had waited for a safe passage. Luo Shan added distribution as a separate question. Publishing a warning, carrying it, and receiving it were three actions that could have different times and different responsible people.

court_rain_heron_log.speaker: rain_heron
court_rain_heron_log.text: My offered entry describes the inner rail, the Heron said, tapping a narrow mark with its beak. I stood under the roof edge and watched the rain crossing the open gap. I had not agreed to keep flying along the exposed spur when the wind rose. The next line says the outer view remained incomplete. That line should travel with the rain description. If someone copies only the description, it sounds as though I watched a whole terrace from everywhere at once. I occupy one body in one place, even when a paper gives me a grander reach.

court_rain_location_word.speaker: narrator
court_rain_location_word.text: One extract called the location terrace; another expanded it to outer terrace in a heading. Neither expansion appeared in the offered log's own location mark. Luo Shan laid the checked sketch beside the words. The Heron confirmed its inner-rail correction, and Zhong Rui confirmed the ordinary names of the roofed and exposed surfaces. Their confirmations served different parts of the map. Lin Yue asked the clerk to amend the heading to the supported location, preserving the earlier wording in correction history. Erasing the mistake would make the current clarity seem older than it really was.

court_rain_witness_discomfort.speaker: narrator
court_rain_witness_discomfort.text: The Heron shook water from one neck feather and looked toward the room's doorway. It disliked being summoned to repair a phrase it had never chosen. Luo Shan acknowledged the cost of explaining the same boundary again. The log's owner could permit a clear correction and then leave further documentary work to the clerks. Attendance at the common hearing remained a separate offer, with its bounded allowance and the option of an equal fish invoice. No payment required the bird to agree with the petition or extend its ordinary weather duties. Its statement belonged to its observations.

court_rain_bulletin_choice.speaker: lin_yue
court_rain_bulletin_choice.text: We need a correction that can survive beyond this room, Lin Yue said. If our insight is sufficient, we can compare every offered location phrase against the map and mark the source beside each change. With the Heron's willing participation, Luo Shan can read the paired passages aloud for a checked statement within this interval. Or we can prepare a plain side-by-side copy and let the authorized clerk verify it against the preserved pages. Each route should retain the earlier wording, identify the actual inner rail, and leave unsupported outer conditions open.

choices.text: Trace offered location phrases through their source references.
Read the complete passages with the Heron's bounded agreement.
Prepare a plain paired copy for the authorized source check.

court_rain_phrase_comparison.speaker: narrator
court_rain_phrase_comparison.text: Lin Yue set three location phrases beneath the corresponding map marks. The offered log named inner rail. The complete revised bulletin preserved the roofed observation boundary. The expanded extract alone used outer terrace. She followed the ink from each phrase to its source, discovering that a heading had been carried across from an older form. That established a documentary route for the error without establishing deliberate deception. Luo Shan entered the source beside each correction. The corrected page would let a later reader repeat the comparison rather than merely accept Lin Yue's interpretation.

court_rain_readback_statement.speaker: narrator
court_rain_readback_statement.text: Luo Shan read the offered passages in their complete order. The Heron interrupted once, asking him to distinguish a mark for observed rain from a mark for increasing pressure. He corrected the spoken reading and the draft statement. The bird then agreed that the statement accurately preserved its offered distinctions. It did not endorse the unrelated accident summary. The authorized clerk witnessed the scope and kept the readback within the agreed interval. Lin Yue saw relief in the Heron's lowered neck when the page finally stopped asking its weather marks to speak about unseen hands.

court_rain_paired_copy.speaker: narrator
court_rain_paired_copy.text: Shen Qing made a plain paired copy of the disputed heading and the complete log passage. He left a wide margin for the authorized clerk's source check and used no interpretive title above the pair. The clerk verified the offered pages, then added the checked map reference. Luo Shan wrote the correction history separately. The plain method took another sheet and more copying time, but it required no additional live explanation from the Heron. When the bird turned toward the window, no one called it back merely to add a decorative signature to a boundary already recorded.

court_rain_bulletin_rejoin.speaker: narrator
court_rain_bulletin_rejoin.text: The resulting correction identified the inner rail, retained the unobserved outer condition, and preserved the route by which the heading had changed. Luo Shan read the correction's claim one last time. It made no finding about the sling's hidden cause. It prevented a weather witness from being assigned a place and a view the offered record did not support. The clerk placed the earlier extract behind the corrected one rather than destroying it. Lin Yue asked that both travel to the hearing, since the disagreement itself explained why the correction had become necessary.

court_rain_revision_reason.speaker: narrator
court_rain_revision_reason.text: The bulletin clerk explained that revisions often combined a forecast with newly received observations. A later sheet could become more specific without proving that the first had been knowingly false. In this case, the offered publication record supported the sequence and the supplied sources, leaving their relationship to the accident's exact minute open. Luo Shan wrote that explanation beside the clerk's own name. He would not turn an office practice into a claim about every revision. Lin Yue noticed a stack of unused old forms and asked that their misleading outer heading be marked before the next notice went out.

court_rain_forecast_separation.speaker: shen_qing
court_rain_forecast_separation.text: The current canal forecast is another document, Shen Qing said. Its Day five closure concern does not belong inside the older accident warning merely because both discuss rain. We should give each notice its date, area, and decision maker. The canal operators may close access if conditions reach their threshold; the forecast is a warning to plan, not a promise that water will obey a date. If these papers are joined without labels, someone may use tomorrow's risk to rewrite yesterday's responsibility. Let the court compare them while keeping their different tasks visible.

court_rain_copied_source.speaker: narrator
court_rain_copied_source.text: Two weather extracts had reached the fault file under different cover sheets. Luo Shan followed their source references and found that both drew from the same offered Heron entry. One preserved the rain phrase; the other preserved the pressure phrase. They were two excerpts, not two independent witnesses. The clerk checked the references and agreed to correct the source count. Lin Yue placed a bracket around the pair and wrote one offered log. The Heron watched the bracket take shape, then asked that its separate refusal to make an unsafe flight remain attached as well.

court_rain_source_count.speaker: luo_shan
court_rain_source_count.text: A second cover does useful handling work, Luo Shan said, but it cannot create a second observer. We will keep both excerpts because they carry different parts of the offered entry. We will also identify their shared source. That correction does not weaken an observation merely because it was copied twice; it changes the amount of independent support the file can claim. Other lower-landing accounts must be evaluated on their own sources and limits. The hearing should see which agreement comes from separate people and which comes from one page arriving through two administrative paths.

court_rain_corrected_comparison.speaker: narrator
court_rain_corrected_comparison.text: The clerk amended the counting note and dated the correction. The original two covers remained behind it, allowing a reviewer to understand why an earlier tally had seemed larger. Luo Shan checked that the correction did not label either excerpt fabricated. The source was genuine within its offered scope; the error lay in counting copies as independence. Lin Yue gathered the complete bulletin, location sketch, and single-source bracket into one sleeve. A separate sleeve held the material traces. Their relation could be discussed at the hearing without making one kind of evidence pretend to be another.

court_rain_bai_weather_question.speaker: narrator
court_rain_bai_weather_question.text: Bai Qun's question concerned the inspection access and the conditions recorded for her assigned landing and guide work. Luo Shan added the corrected weather-source count to the relevant petition page. He did not tell her that a corrected heading settled whether she completed an inspection. It removed one unsupported shortcut from that argument. Lin Yue marked the remaining question for the common findings: what offered evidence places access restrictions and assigned tasks in a reliable sequence? The docket and cost teams might supply parts she had not seen. Her weather packet would remain open to those parts.

court_rain_blank_entry.speaker: narrator
court_rain_blank_entry.text: A blank weather box appeared on a maintenance form beside a completed equipment entry. Shen Qing asked the keeper what the blank meant. The form's instructions allowed weather to be attached separately, and an attachment reference had faded near the binding. A blank box therefore did not immediately prove that no observation existed. The clerk sought the referenced sheet rather than filling the box from memory. Luo Shan recorded the search as pending. Lin Yue kept the blank visible in the copy, since locating an attachment later would need its own source check and correction date.

court_rain_watch_terms.speaker: rain_heron
court_rain_watch_terms.text: My weather agreements specify a safe place and a bounded watch, the Heron said when they returned to the inner rail. They do not give the court every flight I make or every hour I remain awake. A completed watch can provide its offered observations. A refused unsafe extension can leave a gap that must be handled by another method. I will answer for the agreement I made, and I expect the agreement to answer for its limits. If a form requires a view outside them, the form needs changing; my body is not its spare line.

court_rain_handoff_weather.speaker: narrator
court_rain_handoff_weather.text: Zhong Rui brought a fresh blank for the next ordinary observation. It now separated inner-rail rain, outer conditions, instrument state, and unobserved intervals. The Heron inspected the headings and offered one correction: declined should not share a box with instrument failed. Those described different events and called for different responses. Luo Shan relayed the suggestion to the authorized keeper rather than rewriting the official form himself. Lin Yue saw how a small change could make future gaps more legible without claiming to repair every earlier record. The old forms stayed available for review.

court_rain_refusal_cost.speaker: narrator
court_rain_refusal_cost.text: A messenger arrived asking whether the Heron could make one quick circuit outside for the current forecast. The bird refused the exposed flight. The messenger sighed because a clearer view might shorten his next journey, then accepted the answer. Lin Yue asked what information his route actually required. He needed to know whether the covered footpath was presently open, which the route attendant could answer, and whether canal access might change later, which required the bounded forecast. A dangerous flight had looked like one convenient answer to two separate practical questions. They found two safer sources instead.

court_rain_weather_pause.speaker: narrator
court_rain_weather_pause.text: Rain thinned into a silver veil between the cliff and the lower roofs. The Heron stood quietly while the route attendant issued a current passage notice. Lin Yue left its silence unfilled. The packet had already preserved what the bird chose to offer, and another question would not necessarily make the afternoon clearer. Luo Shan brought a cup of warm water for the waiting messenger and then opened the current canal forecast. Their next task was to describe risk over the coming days, including what could change, before anyone built an access promise around a line of printed ink.

court_rain_pressure_entry.speaker: narrator
court_rain_pressure_entry.text: The current forecast lay beneath a transparent stone weight, its corners safe from the draft. Day five appeared in the canal concern line as an estimated decision window, not a commanded closure. Below it, the forecaster had listed cloud movement, recent channel reports, and the missing upper-basin observation. Luo Shan read the missing observation twice. Its absence widened the range of possible conditions. Lin Yue placed a clean sheet beside the notice for present observations, refusing to write over the original. A forecast could change without losing the record of why its earlier version had seemed plausible.

court_rain_present_pressure.speaker: rain_heron
court_rain_present_pressure.text: The air is changing here, the Heron said, lifting the feathers along its neck. That is a local observation in this interval. It supports attention to the next report, not a certain canal height on Day five. The upper basin can receive rain we do not see, and the channel can carry water after this cliff has cleared. I can offer the changes I notice from this safe rail. I cannot give you a perfect map of every cloud, and I will not pretend that refusing an unsafe flight leaves me with nothing useful to say.

court_rain_rising_cloud.speaker: narrator
court_rain_rising_cloud.text: Shen Qing watched a lower cloud seam lift past the arch and disappear behind the court wall. He marked its direction beside the time source, keeping the line short enough to represent only the visible interval. The Heron corrected his word continuous: the cloud had vanished twice behind stone before returning. He changed it to repeatedly rising where visible. Luo Shan asked whether the forecaster's copy could accommodate such ordinary interruptions. It could. The form already had a space for obscured view, but older summaries had often left that space out to fit a smaller sheet.

court_rain_safe_window.speaker: narrator
court_rain_safe_window.text: The route attendant inspected the covered footing after another gust. He allowed passage within the inner line and kept the exposed gate closed. That current decision applied to the path he checked, not the damaged goods lift or every canal below. Lin Yue asked him to name the boundary on the public passage card. He did, then added the condition that another check could pause passage again. The card offered travelers a usable present answer. It also spared the weather witness from being treated as the sole authority for every door and bridge on the cliff.

court_rain_observation_options.speaker: shen_qing
court_rain_observation_options.text: The leveled gauge now works, Shen Qing said. Its present collection can be compared with offered local accounts; upstream news still takes time. One measured discharge into Yue's grounded reference wick can light a safe reading. The keeper can also confirm his scheduled interval, if he agrees, or we can wait and report the delay. None alters rainfall. Keep the wick away from the bottle and preserve its starting allowance. A clearer local mark remains local when the forecaster copies it.

court_rain_forecast_choice.speaker: lin_yue
court_rain_forecast_choice.text: The forecaster needs one present comparison before completing today's revision, Lin Yue said. Our choice concerns how to read this safe instrument and record its source. A screened light may help through the dim interval. A willing keeper may independently confirm the ordinary reading before his next task. Or we can use the gauge's usual schedule, accepting that the revision will leave later. We should make the cost in time visible, keep everyone inside the checked boundary, and send no invented upper-basin result simply because an empty line looks untidy.

choices.text: Read the safe scale with a screened qi lamp.
Request the keeper's bounded ordinary comparison.
Use the scheduled gauge interval and retain the delay.

court_rain_forecast_lamp.speaker: narrator
court_rain_forecast_lamp.text: Zhong Rui set the grounded reference wick beside the safe scale. Lin Yue checked its blank, delivered one quarter-unit through her first arm pair and closed admission. The light lasted only the scheduled reading. Her hand and the wick stayed inside the covered line, clear of the water. Zhong confirmed the level before she discharged. Luo recorded the dose, present interval and earlier controlled pour separately. Local rain had filled the gauge; a visitor's light had only made its divisions readable.

court_rain_forecast_keeper.speaker: narrator
court_rain_forecast_keeper.text: The station keeper agreed to confirm the next ordinary reading from his protected post. He wrote his description before Luo Shan read the terrace result aloud. Their reports concerned different places and did not match exactly. Instead of choosing the larger figure, Luo Shan named each location and interval. The forecaster could consider the difference as a sign that the cliff distributed rain unevenly. The keeper returned to his scheduled work when the check ended. His limited agreement had added one current source, while leaving upstream conditions and the older accident minute unresolved.

court_rain_forecast_schedule.speaker: narrator
court_rain_forecast_schedule.text: They waited for the ordinary gauge interval under the roof. The delay gave the messenger time to finish his warm water and ask about the next passage check. Zhong Rui read the scale when its scheduled mark arrived, using the fixed shade and the corrected mounting. Shen Qing wrote the interval's beginning and end, with the named clock source. The result would reach the forecaster later than a special reading, and the revision noted that cost. No extra keeper was summoned. The method used an established task instead of creating an invisible unpaid duty to accelerate the visitors' page.

court_rain_forecast_rejoin.speaker: narrator
court_rain_forecast_rejoin.text: The authorized forecaster received the present comparison with its named location, interval, and reading method. He placed it beside the offered channel report rather than averaging unrelated figures into one rainfall total. Luo Shan asked him to explain the revised concern line in ordinary language. The forecaster said that access might be restricted around Day five if the expected rise developed, with earlier or later decisions possible as new reports arrived. Lin Yue copied the conditional words carefully. A warning that admitted its range could still guide food, testimony, and travel arrangements.

court_rain_forecast_bounds.speaker: narrator
court_rain_forecast_bounds.text: The revised page listed these influences: unseen upper-basin rainfall, the speed at which channel water arrived, and future access inspections by the operators. Those influences meant the date could move. Luo Shan added the current facts beneath them: the goods lift remained closed, the outer spur remained closed, and the covered footpath had a bounded present passage rule. The page now distinguished known local restrictions from forecast future canal restrictions. Lin Yue asked the forecaster to keep both kinds separately, since a traveler deciding whether to leave now needed another answer from a clerk planning next week's evidence route.

court_rain_upper_basin.speaker: rain_heron
court_rain_upper_basin.text: An empty upper-basin line is worth noticing, the Heron said from the wide sill. You can ask its proper observers for an offered report, provided the route and work are safe. You cannot ask my wings to become every observer's spare instrument. I have given the inner rail and the intervals I agreed to watch. If another place remains unobserved, the forecast should carry that gap until a permitted source arrives. I would rather help you plan for a wider possibility than narrow the page with a flight I do not consent to make.

court_rain_day_five_range.speaker: shen_qing
court_rain_day_five_range.text: We can prepare for a range without pretending all outcomes are equal, Shen Qing said. The forecast gives reasons to expect trouble around Day five, and its limits give reasons to keep checking. A traveler may arrange supplies before then while retaining an alternative if the decision changes. The court's Day seven evidence review is a legal date, not a weather prediction. We should keep those dates separate on the notice. If canal passage fails, local or written testimony remains possible under the existing rule; a storm should not quietly turn an access problem into a forfeited right.

court_rain_operator_authority.speaker: narrator
court_rain_operator_authority.text: The canal operator's public rule described who inspected the channel and who could announce a closure. The forecaster supplied risk information but did not issue that operational order. Luo Shan attached the rule to the notice summary. Lin Yue asked how travelers would learn of a changed decision if they could not return to the court. The operator's local posting stations and ordinary messenger route were listed. Coverage had limits, especially if passage itself closed. The hearing could discuss a bounded paid supplement later, but the weather team would not promise a permanent network from the money presently available.

court_rain_urgent_words.speaker: narrator
court_rain_urgent_words.text: A hurried shopkeeper leaned into the doorway and asked whether all boats would stop on Day five. Luo Shan gave him the revised concern line and the operator's decision rule. The shopkeeper frowned at the conditional words, wanting a single answer for a shipment already wrapped. Lin Yue asked where it needed to go and whether delay would spoil it. His goods were dry tools, not food or medicine. He could plan an earlier departure or await another local notice. The uncertainty still cost him a choice, but it did not require the court to invent a certain storm.

court_rain_notice_choice.speaker: lin_yue
court_rain_notice_choice.text: The revised concern should reach people who can use it, Lin Yue said. We can carefully compare a short public summary against every dated source, ensuring that its certainty never outruns the offered pages. Or Luo Shan can use his existing assistance role to read the notice with the willing local keepers who receive these postings. If those arrangements are unavailable, we can send the complete ordinary notice through its established route and keep the expected delay visible. We should preserve the operator's authority, the Day five range, and the Day seven evidence review in any version.

choices.text: Check a concise public summary against each dated source.
Read the authorized notice with willing local posting keepers.
Send the complete notice through its ordinary route.

court_rain_notice_compare.speaker: narrator
court_rain_notice_compare.text: Lin Yue drafted a short summary, then checked each sentence against the offered page that supported it. She removed a tempting phrase promising five clear days. The forecast had never offered that promise. She also separated present closed fittings from possible future canal restriction, and kept the review date on its own line. The authorized keeper checked the final public wording. Luo Shan retained the comparison marks in the working copy. The shorter notice saved reading time without saving words by discarding the conditions that made its advice trustworthy.

court_rain_notice_readers.speaker: narrator
court_rain_notice_readers.text: Luo Shan read the revised notice with the willing local keepers during their ordinary posting interval. One asked whether possible closure canceled the evidence extension; another asked whether the damaged goods lift was being reopened. He pointed to the separate legal date and present safety rule. Their questions exposed ambiguities in his first short explanation, so he revised it before they carried it onward. The keepers agreed to relay the authorized notice within their existing route. They accepted no added dangerous journey and no obligation to answer technical questions the forecaster had not delegated to them.

court_rain_notice_ordinary.speaker: narrator
court_rain_notice_ordinary.text: Shen Qing placed the complete authorized notice into the ordinary dispatch sleeve. The keeper recorded its expected route and warned that weather could slow delivery. Luo Shan added that limit to the court's receipt. A shorter summary might have traveled more quickly, but the complete version preserved the conditional wording and the separate decision rules. Lin Yue checked that no private log pages had slipped into the sleeve. The public notice did not need the Heron's unrelated observations or any patient's medical detail. It needed a reliable source, a date, and the boundaries of the advice offered.

court_rain_notice_rejoin.speaker: narrator
court_rain_notice_rejoin.text: The notice left through its authorized route, carrying present restrictions, forecast risk, and the evidence review as separate entries. The messenger had a clearer task now: deliver this dated information, report failed passage, and return no invented answer about an unseen channel. Luo Shan gave him the keeper's contact for later operational changes. Lin Yue kept the dispatch receipt with the weather packet. Their work had not removed the storm from the story. It had made the warning more usable and the promise smaller, so the next person would know what still needed checking.

court_rain_safe_routes.speaker: narrator
court_rain_safe_routes.text: Outside, the Heron watched the covered route attendant renew his passage check. The carrying cradles remained separate from the damaged goods lift, and any trip still required staff and medical approval, cancellation options, and rest stops. Lin Yue copied the current rule for the packet rather than assuming tomorrow's conditions would match today's. The bird lowered one wing against a cooler draft and pointed out a growing pocket of mist beneath the arch. The attendant paused movement again. A present local signal could justify a present check even when the Day five forecast remained uncertain.

court_rain_ordinary_needs.speaker: narrator
court_rain_ordinary_needs.text: Waiting travelers gathered beside the witness room while the path was checked. One needed a meal; another needed a dry place to sit. Luo Shan directed them to the existing assistance post and its limited supplies. He did not offer accident compensation from the ninety-six-copper access fund. Its baseline reservations and the single remaining final-plan allowance had separate purposes. Lin Yue helped move a bench away from the dripping doorway. A small ordinary improvement could relieve the wait without pretending to settle Du's injury, Bai's accusation, or the cost of a future weather station.

court_rain_bounded_station.speaker: shen_qing
court_rain_bounded_station.text: The hearing may choose a bounded paid observation plan, Shen Qing said, but its duration, staff limits, and stopping rule must be written before the remaining thirty-two copper is assigned. A station cannot be made perpetual by calling it public service. The Heron's separate willingness must be asked for each offered contribution, and ordinary keepers must know when a new task ends. We can supply locations, intervals, and missing-source questions for that plan. We cannot reserve the same money for weather, another access route, and another set of copies all at once.

court_rain_quiet_interval.speaker: narrator
court_rain_quiet_interval.text: By late afternoon, the inner drain ran in a clear line and the air smelled less metallic. The Heron shook a last drop from its beak. Lin Yue left the covered rail with the packet under her arm and noticed that her sleeve had remained almost dry while the outer stones shone black. That ordinary difference gave the map a bodily meaning. She had walked only one permitted route through a larger weather problem. The other teams would bring their own roads to the common findings, and her packet needed to meet those roads without swallowing them.

court_rain_packet_approach.speaker: narrator
court_rain_packet_approach.text: Luo Shan cleared a final table for the source inventory. Day two's work was nearing its end, and the common hearing would be held on Day three. The complete weather packet now required a concise account that preserved its distinctions without reading every working note aloud. Lin Yue placed the gauge columns, clock bands, location correction, single-source bracket, and revised forecast in order. Each had changed a question. None had secretly become a verdict. They would check the packet's omissions, permissions, and practical costs once more before carrying it to the shared findings.

court_rain_packet_entry.speaker: narrator
court_rain_packet_entry.text: The source inventory began with five sleeves and one empty place at the table. The empty place was for a finding the weather inquiry did not possess: the hidden cause of the sling slip. Lin Yue labeled it unresolved rather than leaving it to be filled by whichever document sounded most authoritative. Luo Shan arranged the offered records around it. The gauge sleeve explained present collection; the clock sleeve explained timing limits; the trace sleeve preserved material descriptions; the log sleeve corrected source and location; the forecast sleeve supported bounded planning. Their arrangement made the missing conclusion visible.

court_rain_inventory_order.speaker: narrator
court_rain_inventory_order.text: Luo Shan read each sleeve's receipt against its contents. A maintenance tracing had been copied twice, and one duplicate could stay with the keeper rather than swell the hearing packet. The original slate, offered log, sealed samples, and supplier corner remained under their respective custody rules. Lin Yue kept only the authorized extracts and checked drawings needed for shared findings. A lighter packet would be easier to carry along the covered route, but they removed no page whose omission would change a claim. The clerk noted which duplicates had been retained elsewhere and how an authorized reviewer could request them.

court_rain_witness_scope.speaker: rain_heron
court_rain_witness_scope.text: My statement should begin with the inner rail, the Heron said. If it begins with the accident, listeners may imagine that I watched the sling. I did not. I offered weather marks from a place I can name, and I described present conditions during your safe comparisons. I corrected the copied heading and the doubled source count. Those are useful things to carry. The court may ask whether they affect another account, but that judgment is not a new memory inside my head. Keep my words close enough to their place that I can recognize them.

court_rain_missing_source.speaker: narrator
court_rain_missing_source.text: Shen Qing inspected the open intervals again. The upper-basin report remained incomplete, the old clock alignment remained unsupported, and one material custody interval had no offered entry. He wrote each gap beside the question it constrained. None became a declaration that all evidence was useless. Some sequences and observations remained well supported. Lin Yue liked the shape of that distinction: the packet could stand on its own legs without claiming to reach across every hole. Luo Shan checked that the common hearing would receive the gaps along with the strongest pages, rather than discovering them only through an opponent's question.

court_rain_final_check_choice.speaker: lin_yue
court_rain_final_check_choice.text: We have time for one final check within the copying interval, Lin Yue said. With sufficient insight, we can trace each conclusion back through the five sleeves and look for an unsupported jump between them. If the offered witnesses agree, Luo Shan can read the short findings and let each correct the part that belongs to their own source. Otherwise, we can compare the packet with its receipts and source labels in ordinary order. Every method should preserve the unresolved cause, the present observation dates, and the boundary between accurate copying and a judgment about truth.

choices.text: Trace every summary conclusion back to its offered exhibit.
Read back the findings with willing source keepers.
Check receipts, source labels, and copy permissions in order.

court_rain_conclusion_check.speaker: narrator
court_rain_conclusion_check.text: Lin Yue drew a line from each summary sentence to its supporting exhibit. One line crossed from current clock disagreement to the older accident time without an offered bridge. She removed the summary's suggestion that the old hour was probably late and replaced it with unsupported exact alignment. Another sentence called the rope wet during the slip; its source described wetness after securing. She corrected that interval too. The changes made the summary less sweeping and more faithful. Luo Shan preserved the rejected wording in the working draft, giving the authorized clerk a clear record of what had been corrected.

court_rain_source_readback.speaker: narrator
court_rain_source_readback.text: Luo Shan read the short findings to willing source keepers within the agreed interval. Zhong Rui corrected a phrase that made the supply receipt sound like direct proof of installation. The Heron asked that its present comparisons not be folded into the older log. The liftkeeper confirmed the clock names but declined to endorse conclusions about the material samples, which he had not examined. Each response stayed beside its own source. Lin Yue revised the summary accordingly. Agreement did useful work when its scope was named, instead of allowing one signature to certify an entire investigation no signer had witnessed.

court_rain_receipt_check.speaker: narrator
court_rain_receipt_check.text: Shen Qing compared every packet sleeve with its receipt, working from the first page to the last. He found an offered-copy label missing from the log extract and a source reference hidden by a fold in the clock band. The clerk repaired both before closing the covers. This ordinary check did not require new witness attendance or a cultivated interpretation of the evidence. It caught handling mistakes that could later obscure permission and provenance. Luo Shan added the completed receipt check to the copying record, and Lin Yue kept the packet dry while the clerk prepared its ordinary receipt marks.

court_rain_final_checks.speaker: narrator
court_rain_final_checks.text: The checked summary now began with the inquiry's location and dates. It described present gauge undercollection, current clock disagreement, separately handled traces, one offered weather source, and a conditional canal forecast. Its last line preserved the unresolved cause and the other teams' independent work. Luo Shan read that line without softening it. Their investigation had produced real findings and still left responsibility for later examination. The clerk attached the corrected source count and location map where a reader would encounter them before the strongest-sounding weather phrases. The packet's order became part of keeping its claims honest.

court_rain_heron_decline.speaker: narrator
court_rain_heron_decline.text: At the inner rail, the Heron declined another request to fly toward the upper basin. The messenger had hoped its departure could fill the forecast's last open line before dusk. Lin Yue pointed him toward the proper local report route and left the bird's refusal intact. The completed offered observations remained usable. A later refusal did not cancel an earlier statement or make the witness hostile to the petition. The Heron settled its feathers and asked whether the weather summary had retained the safe place where it stood. Luo Shan showed it the first sentence, and it nodded.

court_rain_attendance_terms.speaker: luo_shan
court_rain_attendance_terms.text: Your hearing attendance and one separately agreed safe message flight are invited, Luo Shan told the Heron. The baseline reserves five copper, or an equal fish invoice if you agree. This bounded service buys no particular answer, unsafe flight, or seasonal watch. Each contribution needs your permission; weather may prevent a flight. If you decline attendance or conditions prevent it, your offered checked statement remains usable within its limits. I will put the alternatives and safe-flight boundary on the invitation so a missing body or canceled journey is not mistaken for withdrawn evidence.

court_rain_bai_review.speaker: narrator
court_rain_bai_review.text: Bai Qun's reply arrived through the assistance post. She welcomed the separated equipment remits but objected to a phrase suggesting that unresolved cause made the accusation harmless. The work bar and civil assessment had already affected her, even while the current emergency stay protected her from their immediate disputed operation. Luo Shan changed the phrase. Unresolved did not mean without consequences. Lin Yue kept Bai's objection beside the summary as a party's relevant response. The court would need to examine the accusation and its burden, not merely admire the weather team's careful uncertainty.

court_rain_du_review.speaker: narrator
court_rain_du_review.text: Du Heng's offered response asked that the injury remain visible when the packet discussed uncertain mechanics. His right shoulder still needed restricted lifting, rest, and ordinary review. A cause not yet established did not make the pain imaginary or restore wages automatically. Luo Shan added that practical point without declaring compensation from the access fund. Du's corrected public proof remained admitted; a copied temporary-license annex could not silently take that standing away. Lin Yue saw how the same word unresolved could trouble both parties for different reasons. The hearing had to keep both reasons in view.

court_rain_easy_blame.speaker: narrator
court_rain_easy_blame.text: A waiting observer suggested that the clerk who copied the outer heading should simply pay the disputed assessment. Shen Qing asked what evidence linked that documentary error to the sling's mechanical slip or the injury. None had been offered. The observer looked frustrated, having hoped one visible mistake could absorb the whole case. Luo Shan preserved the correction while rejecting the shortcut. A filing error could require repair, explanation, and accountability within its own scope. It could not become a convenient substitute for an unproved physical cause just because the person responsible was available in the room.

court_rain_planning_value.speaker: lin_yue
court_rain_planning_value.text: Luo Shan placed Bai's objection beside Du's response and reached for a single heading. Lin Yue stopped his pencil. Bai wanted the disputed accusation examined without its existing burden being treated as harmless; Du wanted his ongoing injury and interrupted wages kept visible. A heading called uncertainty alone would conceal both practical requests. They gave each a separate line and attached the offered source. The next table space remained for the other teams' findings. Lin Yue asked the clerk to preserve those party lines in the hearing copy, so technical caution would arrive alongside the reasons anyone needed a decision.

court_rain_duty_form.speaker: narrator
court_rain_duty_form.text: The authorized keeper returned a draft observation form reflecting the offered corrections. It separated location, interval, instrument condition, witness permission, and unobserved area. Luo Shan marked it draft, leaving approval to the responsible office. The Heron's suggested distinction between declined and failed had been included. Zhong Rui wanted a separate space for a pending countersignature so completed cleaning would not conceal an unfinished check. Lin Yue asked that the older forms remain available for comparison. Improving future records could prevent a repeated ambiguity without rewriting the history that made the improvement necessary.

court_rain_keeper_dissent.speaker: narrator
court_rain_keeper_dissent.text: The liftkeeper disliked the additional form space, fearing that every ordinary round would now take twice as long. Zhong Rui defended the separate instrument fields because he had just watched a clean but tilted cup mislead readers. Luo Shan asked each to estimate the added time during an actual bounded round rather than argue from a stack of blank sheets. They agreed to trial the draft under ordinary paid conditions before adopting it. Lin Yue left their disagreement in the note. A clearer record had a labor cost, and acknowledging that cost made the proposed improvement more credible.

court_rain_packet_boundaries.speaker: luo_shan
court_rain_packet_boundaries.text: The hearing copy carries only offered extracts and relevant public rules, Luo Shan said. Nesting pages, unrelated consignments, private family notes, and medical details beyond attendance limits remain with their proper keepers. Accurate certification identifies a faithful copy; it does not make the magistrate omniscient or supply a view no witness had. Our cliff court is its own institution, separate from the fate of Azure Cloud. He Lian must work within its charter and the evidence offered. I will make those source limits readable before the hearing asks anyone to answer a broader question.

court_rain_departures.speaker: narrator
court_rain_departures.text: The Heron left the inner rail for an ordinary sheltered roost of its choosing. It offered no further flight and carried its original log away in a waterproof case held beneath one wing. Zhong Rui checked the corrected gauge before ending his shift. The liftkeeper returned his clock book to the appointed cabinet. Lin Yue watched the different keepers depart with different originals. Their packet held useful copies, while ownership and responsibility remained distributed among living people. A hearing could gather those relations for examination without needing to seize every object into one towering room.

court_rain_chronology_summary.speaker: narrator
court_rain_chronology_summary.text: Luo Shan wrote the route chronology on the cover. Day zero: present gauge comparison, repair-source inquiry, and location map. Day one: current clock comparison and safely offered material traces. Day two: bulletin correction, single-source weather count, conditional forecast, and packet review. The accident remained Day minus two; the gauge-support replacement was recorded Day minus one. Day three would bring the common hearing, while uncertain Day five canal risk and Day seven evidence review remained different future dates. Lin Yue checked that each day belonged to the action actually described, preventing the narrative itself from becoming another misleading clock.

court_rain_exhibit_receipt.speaker: narrator
court_rain_exhibit_receipt.text: The authorized clerk issued the final receipt for the hearing copy. It named the five sleeves, the corrected covers retained behind them, and the keepers of the originals. Luo Shan signed for carrying that copy in his assistance role, without claiming independent power to certify it or rule on its meaning. Lin Yue took a second plain inventory for the shared findings table. If another team cited a source she had not examined, she could now ask for its keeper and boundary in the same terms. The packet had given her questions as useful as its answers.

court_rain_evening_storm.speaker: narrator
court_rain_evening_storm.text: Rain returned in broad strokes across the outer stones as evening deepened. Shen Qing held the hearing copy beneath his coat while Lin Yue checked the sheltered footing with the route attendant. They waited through a short pause, then moved only when passage was renewed. The closed goods lift and exposed spur remained outside their route. No final glimpse was worth risking the packet or their bodies. From inside the arch, they heard the ordinary drain continue its work. The sound was small compared with the clouds, but it belonged to a repair whose limits they actually understood.

court_rain_return_approach.speaker: narrator
court_rain_return_approach.text: They reached the hall's covered antechamber with the packet dry. The room waited for Day three, its benches arranged beneath a pale opening onto the cloud. Lin Yue set the inventory on the shared findings table rather than on the magistrate's empty seat. The docket and access teams would bring independent work before any final choice. She had directly followed one road through the case, and the hall required more than her road. Luo Shan placed a note beside the sleeves inviting source questions, corrections, and the parties' preserved objections. Their careful packet would still need to meet living disagreement.

court_rain_acknowledgment.speaker: luo_shan
court_rain_acknowledgment.text: I will report the weather findings as offered evidence, Luo Shan said. The gauge comparison improves future readings. The clock bands limit old timing claims. The map and source bracket correct the witness file. The forecast supports bounded planning while leaving its date conditional. Bai's assigned work and Du's ongoing injury remain questions the hearing must address with the other teams' records. The remaining thirty-two copper may support one final plan after the baseline reservations, and our route has spent none of it by implication. Let the common table decide with the costs and the unresolved points visible.

court_rain_packet_exit.speaker: narrator
court_rain_packet_exit.text: Lin Yue untied the carrying cord and laid it beside the receipt. The rain beyond the opening had become a soft gray sheet, concealing the lower roofs but leaving the hall's threshold clear. She remembered the Heron's insistence that one body could occupy only one place. Her own investigation had the same limit. Its discoveries were real, its gaps remained, and neither could stand in for the independent work approaching from the other routes. When the shared findings began, she would place both discoveries and gaps before the others, then listen for what their evidence changed.

court_cost_entry.speaker: narrator
court_cost_entry.text: The cost office occupied the lowest room of the court above the rain. Its windows faced the lift ropes rather than the clouds. Lin Yue entered behind a porter carrying four empty witness chairs. Each chair had a brass tally tied beneath its seat, and each tally named a participant and appointment day. The porter set them down without charging for the journey. Across the room, a clerk crossed out a number on the hearing assistance board. Lin Yue waited until the clerk finished the stroke before asking what had changed.

court_cost_board.speaker: narrator
court_cost_board.text: Luo Shan was thirty-nine, with ink collected along the edge of one thumbnail. He had written petitions for fourteen years and knew how much a page cost before anyone called it evidence. The crossed-out number was an estimate, he explained. Bai Qun could no longer use the exposed stair, and the carrying-chair supervisor had submitted an assisted fare. He slid the old estimate beneath the new one instead of destroying it. A court that hid its first price could always pretend nobody had planned their journey around it.

court_cost_scope.speaker: narrator
court_cost_scope.text: Lin Yue placed the city's certified record beside the new landing-incident file. The corrected permanent proofs had already been admitted. No fee dispute here could make those corrections disappear. This case concerned Bai Qun's alleged missed inspection, Du Heng's injured right shoulder, and disputed responsibility for the goods-sling accident two days earlier. Luo Shan nodded toward a second bundle, tied in yellow. That bundle contained the cost of bringing evidence before the court. They would need both bundles, but a paid chair and a proven accusation were different things.

court_cost_invitation.speaker: narrator
court_cost_invitation.text: The court's invitation named Bai Qun and Du Heng, offered statement appointments, and said nothing about the climb. Bai had sent back a practical question about the stairs. Du had asked how much of a working day the journey would consume. Neither reply conceded the disputed assessment. Both were questions from people who had agreed to describe their own work and still had duties waiting below. Luo Shan copied the questions onto separate slips. An invitation became more useful when someone could answer it without borrowing from a household's next meal.

court_cost_he_lian.speaker: narrator
court_cost_he_lian.text: He Lian examined the invitation's blank lower margin. The magistrate looked about sixty-two, though the court staff disagreed about which century had first given her gray eyebrows. She did not explain the omission by invoking tradition. The margin had space enough for fares and expected time, she said, and tomorrow's summons would use it. That correction could help later witnesses. It would not reimburse anyone who had already paid. She asked Luo Shan to bring her the older expenses, with dates, before proposing which office ought to answer for them.

court_cost_old_price.speaker: narrator
court_cost_old_price.text: Mei Dulan produced the city's forwarding receipt. The registry had paid to certify its earlier hearing record, not to buy a favorable decision in this new case. Its receipt covered paper, seal wax, and the copying clerk's afternoon. Two working extracts were now needed from different incident records. Those were genuinely new tasks. A third notice demanded admission preparation under an impressive heading. Mei had not paid it. She wanted to know whether that line described additional work or merely repeated a service the court's appointed staff already owed the hearing.

court_cost_cashbox.speaker: narrator
court_cost_cashbox.text: The assistance cashbox rested on a shelf lower than the magistrate's ceremonial bell. It was plain oak with a split corner repaired by two iron straps. Luo Shan opened it with the cashier present and counted its sealed rolls onto a mat. Ninety-six copper had been assigned from the existing court appropriation for this hearing's access costs. Other petitioners had separate entries on the monthly list. Lin Yue watched the cashier read the authorization before releasing a coin. This hearing's money would have a source, a limit, and a receipt.

court_cost_not_compensation.speaker: narrator
court_cost_not_compensation.text: Luo Shan wrote ASSISTANCE across the top of the working page. This account could buy independent carrying-chair access, pay a necessary attendant, or preserve a court exhibit while the hearing continued. It could not compensate every lost booking, purchase a license, or repay a disputed commercial bond without a ruling. The court had separate authority for those matters. Lin Yue asked whether unused assistance could become compensation. The cashier shook her head. It would return to the appropriation. A bounded fund might be frustrating, but relabeling it would only hide the shortage.

court_cost_porter.speaker: narrator
court_cost_porter.text: The porter returned to collect the chairs after their brass tallies had been checked. He was paid by the court for moving its furniture. A witness sitting in one of those chairs would not owe him a second fee. The clerk marked that distinction on the board, then hesitated over the phrase personal carrying service. The porter pointed to the ropes outside. Furniture could travel as freight. A person needed a supervised carrying chair along the covered footpath, attendants, and room to decline. Those services were a different account.

court_cost_witness_letters.speaker: narrator
court_cost_witness_letters.text: Lin Yue read Bai's reply again. She could climb a short stair with pauses but could not manage the long exposed rise in rain. Her letter requested access rather than treatment and supplied no history beyond what the journey required. Du's bandaged right shoulder made a handrail difficult to use. He wanted to return before his household's evening work began. Luo Shan underlined return before evening. That requirement would shape a useful reservation. It would not justify hurrying an unsafe descent or treating an injured porter as another item of freight.

court_cost_three_accounts.speaker: narrator
court_cost_three_accounts.text: Three account headings appeared beneath the first: journey, hearing work, and keeping exhibits. Luo Shan ruled a line before each heading. Journey contained fares and necessary rest. Hearing work contained actual hours, including interpretation if the court required it. Keeping exhibits contained storage and handling, beginning when the court accepted custody. He left lost city income in the commercial appeal bundle. Costs could affect whether someone reached a hearing without themselves proving the claim being heard. Lin Yue copied the headings, grateful for a distinction she could follow across an untidy desk.

court_cost_writer_fee.speaker: narrator
court_cost_writer_fee.text: His own fee came next. Luo Shan charged for private drafting work according to a posted schedule, but the court paid his appointed assistance hours from its staff account. He could not charge the petitioners for those same hours. He showed Lin Yue an appointment slip, then his private work book, with today's morning crossed into the staff column. In the afternoon he had promised a merchant an unrelated petition. If this inquiry overran, he would have to reschedule that work or surrender its fee. The handwriting stayed the same in both columns.

court_cost_missing_assumptions.speaker: narrator
court_cost_missing_assumptions.text: The first estimate assumed Bai and Du would arrive together, use one ordinary goods journey, and finish their statements before the noon meal. The invitation had never stated those assumptions. Bai's stone yard could release her on Day1, while Du had arranged household help for Day2. They required a supervised carrying chair, not the descending freight sling involved in the accident. Luo Shan drew two timelines beneath the estimate. Nobody had lied about their availability. They had simply been priced as a group before anyone asked when they could travel safely.

court_cost_clerk_resistance.speaker: narrator
court_cost_clerk_resistance.text: The estimating clerk, a woman named Dai, watched Luo Shan redraw the page. Dai had priced dozens of small hearings using the cheaper freight line because petitioners usually climbed alongside their bundles. She disliked being treated as careless for following the old worksheet. Luo Shan asked her to bring the board, not an apology. Dai fetched it herself. Its freight fare excluded occupied passenger service. Lin Yue placed the two timelines beside that sentence. Saving money would require a journey people could actually use, rather than a smaller number written over their lives.

court_cost_question_hub.speaker: narrator
court_cost_question_hub.text: They could begin by checking the chair-service schedule, comparing the notices for copying work, or checking the cashier's remaining authority over reserved funds. Dai favored the cashier. The porter favored the path, where the afternoon rain was already thickening. Luo Shan would record all three inquiries, whichever Lin Yue joined first. She noticed that each person had given a reason tied to their work. There was no perfect place to begin. There was only a first uncertainty they could resolve before another clerk made tomorrow's estimate from it.

court_cost_begin_lift.speaker: narrator
court_cost_begin_lift.text: Lin Yue chose the chair board because the weather could close its covered path before the clerks closed their books. The porter took her to the path shelter and introduced the chair supervisor. Luo Shan sent Dai to verify the cashier's authority in parallel and kept the copying notices on his own desk. They agreed to bring their findings back before changing the hearing estimate. From the shelter, the covered path looked level and endless. Rain blowing beneath its roof was enough to remind Lin Yue that a line on paper had to survive wind.

court_cost_begin_notices.speaker: narrator
court_cost_begin_notices.text: Lin Yue chose the copying notices because one had already reached the city and might be paid before anyone corrected it. Luo Shan compared the dates while Dai took the authority question to the cashier. The porter agreed to obtain the chair timetable and bring back the supervisor's current fare. Nobody waited for Lin Yue to supervise an inquiry she had not chosen. The admission preparation notice used heavier paper than the registry receipt. Its impressive heading covered three small lines, one of which named a service the court's invitation had already promised.

court_cost_begin_authority.speaker: narrator
court_cost_begin_authority.text: Lin Yue chose the cashier's reserve authority because a cheap later plan was useless if the money could not lawfully pay for it. Dai led her to the appropriation desk with the previous monthly order. Luo Shan began checking the copying notices, and the porter went for the chair timetable. Before they separated, Lin Yue asked each to record unanswered questions alongside confirmed prices. The cashier greeted Dai by name. Her desk held many small petitions, all requesting modest sums that became substantial when stacked together. She cleared a space without removing anyone else's request.

court_cost_reports_first.speaker: narrator
court_cost_reports_first.text: By the time the rain struck the window sideways, all three inquiries had produced a first answer. The chair supervisor had confirmed separate departure needs. The cashier had found the current assistance order, including its remaining reserve. Luo Shan had identified one genuinely new copying task and another already covered by the court's appointed clerk. Each answer made the estimate less tidy. Dai brought fresh paper rather than squeezing alterations into the original. They would keep the original beside it, so the Day3 common hearing could see both the planning mistake and the attempt to correct it.

court_cost_rain_heron.speaker: narrator
court_cost_rain_heron.text: The Rain Heron landed on the rope shelter with a slate strapped beneath one wing. Its long feet made quiet taps on the roof tiles. It inspected the closed goods-sling approach each morning because falling water sometimes hid a loose guide ring. The court paid for those inspections in fish and a sheltered resting perch, by a season's agreement. Today's slate recorded an extra examination after a gust. The heron laid it where the keeper could read it. A paid safety check was part of making a journey possible, whether anyone found the bird beautiful or not.

court_cost_check_scope.speaker: narrator
court_cost_check_scope.text: The goods-lift keeper explained what the heron's marks could establish. It had observed approach ropes and the guide ring from outside during permitted inspection. It had not examined every hidden brake fitting, and the equipment remained closed. The marks described work, not an operating clearance. Lin Yue requested today's offered public maintenance entry. The keeper provided it from the board. They needed neither the heron's private hunting route nor a promise about tomorrow's wind to distinguish inspection labor from hearing attendance. The independent carrying-chair service used the covered footpath, entirely separate from the goods lift.

court_cost_passenger_board.speaker: narrator
court_cost_passenger_board.text: The carrying-chair board priced an assisted round trip at eight copper. That bought supervised ascent along the covered footpath, a booked return that day, safe rest stops, and trained carriers. It used no part of the closed counterweighted goods lift and promised no journey during unsafe conditions. Dai copied the whole line. Beside it she wrote Bai, Day1, and Du, Day2. Two reservations meant sixteen copper. The larger number finally described a service someone could actually receive. Empty-chair repositioning was included, with a separate supervisor responsible for the path and team.

court_cost_bai_date.speaker: narrator
court_cost_bai_date.text: Bai's reservation could begin after the stone yard's morning count. The chair supervisor proposed a later ascent than the court's first invitation had named, leaving room for Bai to reach the lower landing without running. Her statement appointment would move with it. Lin Yue expected the clerk to complain about changing the court's hour. Instead, Dai found a later morning space and wrote carefully between two existing appointments. The court had wanted Bai's account of an inspection. Making her miss another working obligation without asking would have been a poor way to obtain it.

court_cost_du_date.speaker: narrator
court_cost_du_date.text: Du's appointment belonged on Day2. He had arranged for a neighbor to help with household lifting that morning, and changing the day would unravel that arrangement. The chair supervisor asked whether Du could sit upright with his right arm supported. Luo Shan would send the question rather than supply an answer from the bandage mentioned in the record. A handcart could take him across the lower approach, but the carrying chair itself still required a safe seated position. A paid reservation would remain a reservation if he could not make the transfer. Nobody called that wasted evidence.

court_cost_return_ticket.speaker: narrator
court_cost_return_ticket.text: Luo Shan asked what happened if a statement ended after the reserved descent. The chair supervisor pointed to the next safe covered-path return and its available team. A same-day return within that reservation would not add a fare, but overnight lodging was outside the eight copper. The court therefore needed a short statement appointment and a clear stopping time. Luo Shan marked those requirements beneath each reservation. He could pause a transcript and arrange later questions in writing. He could not promise that the covered path would stay open because his pen had not reached the bottom of a page.

court_cost_lift_staff.speaker: narrator
court_cost_lift_staff.text: The goods-lift keeper was Sui Dan, forty-seven. His ordinary duty account covered the closed equipment's inspection and records, not the independently staffed carrying chairs. Tomorrow's testimony involved different work: explaining his offered entries after his normal shift, with the relevant log available. Five copper covered that bounded hour. Lin Yue wrote maintenance duty and testimony on different lines. Sui had feared that payment for speaking would make his ordinary work seem bought twice. The chair supervisor retained a separate service account. Neither payment promised agreement about the accident or reopened the closed machinery.

court_cost_weight_limit.speaker: narrator
court_cost_weight_limit.text: The chair supervisor brought out the carrying team's capacity and rest schedule. A separate goods-lift freight card described a different machine. Lin Yue compared them because Dai's first estimate had treated a person as freight, leaving causation to the maintenance and weather inquiries. A cheaper goods category was no available passenger service. Dai copied both headings onto her worksheet and preserved her first estimate. The hearing would see where the wrong category had entered the arithmetic before correction. The carrying-chair journey required its own staff checks and had no connection to operating the closed goods lift.

court_cost_handcart_quote.speaker: narrator
court_cost_handcart_quote.text: At the lower landing, a handcart keeper offered a short assisted transfer for four copper. It included the sheltered route between the arrival path and the carrying chair, a waiting bench, and one attendant for the booked transfer. It did not include hauling commercial cargo or tending an injury after the journey. Bai and Du would each have an allocation, eight copper together. The keeper showed a repaired wheel before taking any booking. Its spokes were uneven, but the axle turned cleanly. Lin Yue asked the travelers to approve the proposed assistance before releasing payment.

court_cost_lift_choice.speaker: narrator
court_cost_lift_choice.text: Three points still needed checking before the reservations became useful. The court could compare the actual handcart route with its description, ask the supervisor to rehearse an empty-chair transfer, or revise the appointment times beside Dai. Lin Yue could accompany one check while the others were recorded by the people doing them. The supervisor offered the empty-chair rehearsal without adding a fee; it was a normal service check. The handcart keeper wanted an answer before another customer booked the morning. A modest price still needed a definite task, a person, and an hour.

court_cost_cart_check.speaker: narrator
court_cost_cart_check.text: Lin Yue walked the handcart route with its keeper. One corner had pooled rain deep enough to hide a broken paving edge. The keeper chose the covered detour and measured its extra length with ordinary strides. It remained within the quoted four copper, but required an earlier arrival at the path. Dai added that time to the invitation. No traveler had to perform this check for the court. When the keeper reached the waiting bench, he dried its seat with a cloth he carried for his own customers and showed where an attendant could stand without blocking the chair transfer.

court_cost_cradle_check.speaker: narrator
court_cost_cradle_check.text: Lin Yue watched the carrying team place its empty chair level beside the waiting bench. The supervisor demonstrated the supported transfer and identified who would lift, guide, and call a stop. The handcart attendant retained a separate lower-approach task. Nobody put a wounded person inside for a trial. This rehearsal concerned today's access service and left the earlier goods accident unresolved. Dai recorded the sequence beside the price. Eight copper now corresponded to actions they could check before payment, without touching the closed counterweighted equipment or asking it to carry a person.

court_cost_time_check.speaker: narrator
court_cost_time_check.text: Lin Yue sat beside Dai while she moved the appointments. Each traveler needed arrival time, a brief rest, one bounded statement hour, and the booked return. Luo Shan divided his assistance work accordingly. He would prepare questions beforehand, record what each person offered, and leave further requests for a separately scheduled response. The ordinary clerk would handle the transcript under the existing staff account. Dai changed the invitation from attend until released to attend within this appointment. Lin Yue watched that small revision turn an open-ended summons into a day someone could plan around.

court_cost_lift_return.speaker: narrator
court_cost_lift_return.text: The three checks returned to Luo Shan's table. The handcart would use a covered detour, the chair transfer had been rehearsed empty, and the statement appointments now fitted the scheduled returns. Bai would travel on Day1 and Du on Day2, subject to the supervisor's safety decision. Sixteen copper covered their two round trips; eight covered their lower-landing assistance. No third ascent had been funded. Their authorized records could be used at the common Day3 hearing. Luo Shan sent that point with the revised invitations so neither traveler would mistake a later court date for another compulsory journey.

court_cost_sui_boundary.speaker: narrator
court_cost_sui_boundary.text: The chair supervisor read the revised invitation before the messenger left. It said that the supervisor could postpone under the chair-service rules. He wanted that line kept even if it made the court's schedule awkward. The magistrate's earlier stay of the disputed assessment did not certify the landing physically safe. Dai copied the line without argument. She had begun the morning trying to make four accounts look smaller. By afternoon, she was making each account say what it could actually buy. The supervisor signed only the fare and service terms, not the truth of anyone's testimony.

court_cost_heron_attendance.speaker: narrator
court_cost_heron_attendance.text: The Rain Heron studied its bounded service slip. Seasonal inspection work remained under its separate agreement. Five copper covered the agreed hearing participation and one safe message flight if separately accepted under its route terms; neither required a particular answer or unsafe passage. It chose an equivalent fish invoice instead of coins. The cashier would pay once, recording what occurred and returning unused sums under the service terms. The bird tapped the separate word inspection on its older contract. Lin Yue kept both papers visible. No payment bought further flights or a standing right to summon the spirit.

court_cost_fish_supplier.speaker: narrator
court_cost_fish_supplier.text: The fish supplier brought a narrow basket and a priced list, not a promise to feed the heron indefinitely. Five copper bought the listed portion on the agreed day. If weather prevented delivery, the supplier would offer another safe collection time or return the payment. The heron chose the latter condition in writing. Its beak left a small dark mark beside the clause. Dai had never prepared a witness payment that ended in a basket, but the cashier accepted an ordinary supplier invoice. A spirit's preferred payment still needed the same finite arithmetic as everyone else's.

court_cost_empty_cradle.speaker: narrator
court_cost_empty_cradle.text: An empty carrying chair went down the covered path as its supervisor checked tomorrow's team schedule. Lin Yue remembered the goods sling in Du's account and kept the services separate. Chair reservations, freight records, and maintenance testimony each belonged to their own question. She returned the capacity pages to their rack. Below, the handcart keeper waited for corrected times. That keeper needed to know when a paying task began and which tasks the price excluded. The court's preliminary stay did not certify equipment safe, and these independent journeys would never imply the goods lift had reopened.

court_cost_appointment_reply.speaker: narrator
court_cost_appointment_reply.text: A messenger returned with Bai's acceptance of the Day1 appointment and Du's acceptance of the Day2 appointment. Bai approved the handcart assistance after reading the covered-route description. Du asked that the waiting bench remain available if the transfer strained his right shoulder. The chair supervisor confirmed that request within the existing quote. Neither letter accepted the disputed incident assessment or withdrew a claim for lost work. Luo Shan filed the replies with access papers rather than the merits bundle. A person's agreement to travel could establish the journey's terms without being stretched into agreement about the accident.

court_cost_weather_cancel.speaker: narrator
court_cost_weather_cancel.text: Dai asked how the reservations would be accounted for if unsafe rain canceled an ascent. The supervisor's published rule returned the unused passenger fare; the handcart keeper charged only an actually provided transfer. A statement appointment could move or proceed through another authorized form of evidence. The court would not describe the cancellation as Bai refusing examination or Du abandoning his claim. Luo Shan put those terms on the worksheet before anyone needed them. The Day5 canal forecast was uncertain. A workable plan needed ordinary cancellation rules rather than a special excuse invented after the water had risen.

court_cost_first_subtotal.speaker: narrator
court_cost_first_subtotal.text: Luo Shan wrote the journey subtotal beneath the corrected worksheet: sixteen for two assisted carrying-chair round trips, eight for two lower-landing transfers, twenty for four bounded attendance allocations. Forty-four copper. The last line covered Bai, Du, Sui, and the Rain Heron at five each, with the heron's agreed fish invoice counting once. Their accounts might differ sharply when the hearing asked about the accident. Nothing in the payment terms rewarded agreement. Luo Shan drew a line below forty-four and left room for copying and storage, the two remaining baseline costs still to be checked.

court_cost_record_table.speaker: narrator
court_cost_record_table.text: On the next table lay the two records requiring working extracts. One was the incident-and-maintenance log accepted from the lower landing. The other was the relevant wage and verification annex, including the copied temporary-license reference whose effect the court had already limited. The originals had their own keepers and permissions. The hearing needed certified excerpts of the offered entries, not a new ownership claim over entire books. Luo Shan had placed blank paper between the bundles. Lin Yue asked the certifying clerk to explain which work the proposed eight-copper copying cost would actually include.

court_cost_clerk_seal.speaker: narrator
court_cost_clerk_seal.text: The certifying clerk was named Ru Fang. He had custody of the court's copy seal during his shift and no authority to change an offered entry. Four copper bought one checked working extract, its page materials, and the second clerk's comparison against the source. The price did not depend on whether the entry helped Bai, Du, or the lift staff. Ru Fang showed the place where the original keeper would acknowledge the comparison. Luo Shan would assist with the request, but his petition writer's mark could not substitute for the clerks' certification.

court_cost_copy_extent.speaker: narrator
court_cost_copy_extent.text: Lin Yue asked whether an extract could omit surrounding entries that made its meaning uncertain. Ru Fang said the offered scope would determine that question before copying began. A date heading and an adjacent correction might belong with the selected entry. Unrelated workers' addresses did not. The source keeper could attend the comparison or permit the defined pages to be viewed under the custody terms. Luo Shan wrote the proposed boundaries on a request rather than guessing them from a folded corner. Paying for a smaller copy should not produce a misleading quotation of a larger record.

court_cost_annex_context.speaker: narrator
court_cost_annex_context.text: Mei identified the copied temporary-license reference in the wage annex. The new court case had used it to delay verification, although the permanent proofs had already been corrected and admitted.
