That reference needed to remain visible beside the court's preliminary correction, not vanish from the historical page. Ru Fang would copy both within the offered scope. The extract would show what the record had said and what the court had changed before these inquiries. It would not transform an improper verification obstacle into evidence that Bai missed an inspection or Du caused his own injury.

court_cost_log_context.speaker: narrator
court_cost_log_context.text: The maintenance log presented a different problem. A cramped entry referred to a separate job slip, and the keeper had offered that slip's relevant face with the log. Lin Yue could not tell whether the smaller writing had been squeezed in at the time or added later. She left the question to the source comparison rather than turning poor handwriting into an accusation. Ru Fang included the visible reference on his request. The extract would preserve an uncertainty the hearing needed to examine, including the fact that one page could not answer it alone.

court_cost_duplicate_notice.speaker: narrator
court_cost_duplicate_notice.text: Luo Shan brought the admission preparation notice back into view. It asked for six copper to arrange the petition's ordinary place in the docket. The court had already assigned that staff task and admitted the corrected proofs without requiring a private payment. The notice was a private writer's offer attached to an outdated worksheet. It was not a clerk's demand. Luo Shan could say so from the appointment order, but he would ask the court clerk to issue the correction. Petition writers could sell useful work; this particular service was unnecessary for the access already granted.

court_cost_private_writer.speaker: narrator
court_cost_private_writer.text: The private writer came when Dai asked him to explain his notice. His name was Jian Bo, and he had copied the older form because petitioners often wanted help organizing bundles. He did not claim that six copper belonged to the court. He agreed that the heading could suggest a required admission service and replaced it with voluntary bundle arrangement. No money had changed hands. Lin Yue kept both versions. A corrected offer could prevent the next misunderstanding without proving Jian had intended to deceive everyone who saw an impressive heading.

court_cost_dai_admission.speaker: narrator
court_cost_dai_admission.text: Dai acknowledged that she had clipped Jian's notice behind the court invitation without explaining the difference. She had thought another pair of hands would make the hearing file arrive neatly. Bai and Du might instead have read the combined papers as one required bill. Ru Fang wrote an official clarification that ordinary docket arrangement was covered by the court's staff account. Dai would send it with the corrected transport terms. Lin Yue watched her test the new wording aloud. It named the service already available and left the private writer free to offer genuinely additional work.

court_cost_copy_choice.speaker: narrator
court_cost_copy_choice.text: The clerks could now check the incident extract against its offered source, check the wage annex's correction history, or compare the old and revised service notices for the court's outgoing letters. Lin Yue would join one task while Ru Fang and Mei supervised the other defined comparisons. The two paid extracts remained the same two extracts regardless of where she stood. Luo Shan put the requests beside their price lines. A thorough check would need attention, but the fund did not become larger simply because three useful questions were laid on a table together.

court_cost_copy_log.speaker: narrator
court_cost_copy_log.text: Lin Yue watched the log comparison from the side of the table. The keeper indicated the offered date heading, the incident entry, and the job-slip reference without surrendering unrelated pages. Ru Fang read the proposed extract back slowly. Where an abbreviation remained uncertain, he preserved it and added a descriptive note approved for that comparison. Neither clerk silently expanded it into a technical conclusion. Lin Yue understood less about the machine than before, but more about the limits of this paper. The hearing would receive the uncertainty rather than a polished sentence someone had invented to conceal it.

court_cost_copy_annex.speaker: narrator
court_cost_copy_annex.text: Lin Yue joined Mei at the wage annex. She placed the corrected proof acknowledgment beside the earlier license reference and showed Ru Fang their distinct dates. The clerks copied the relevant entries in order. No worker's permanent proof became commercial collateral again because an older annex had repeated the wrong identifier. The extract retained that older error as history and marked the current admission status clearly. Lin Yue watched the copy dry before it was checked. A document could preserve the path of a mistake while making it difficult for the next clerk to repeat the mistake as present authority.

court_cost_copy_notices.speaker: narrator
court_cost_copy_notices.text: Lin Yue compared the old notice packet with the outgoing corrections. The new letter named the two four-copper extracts, stated that ordinary admission preparation required no private fee, and explained what appointed staff would do. Luo Shan removed an ornamental sentence that praised the court's generosity. The correction was owed because its own packet had been unclear. Dai wrote the addresses on the outside and asked Lin Yue to check them before sealing. No customer addresses from the wage annex were needed to send Bai and Du their personal replies. The clerks used the contact details each petitioner had supplied.

court_cost_copy_rejoin.speaker: narrator
court_cost_copy_rejoin.text: The source comparisons and notice review returned to the same page. Eight copper covered two certified extracts; the optional private arrangement offer had no place in the required budget. The court clerk sent the clarification through the ordinary outgoing post. No access-fund money paid Jian for withdrawing an unnecessary offer or Dai for correcting her packet. Those tasks belonged to their existing responsibilities. Luo Shan wrote the copying subtotal beneath the forty-four already planned for journey and attendance. Fifty-two copper now had defined baseline uses. Storage would determine the remaining twelve before the reserve could be considered.

court_cost_mei_pause.speaker: narrator
court_cost_mei_pause.text: Mei asked to sit for a moment after the copies were finished. The familiar mistaken identifier had made her expect another long fight over public proofs. This time the court's preliminary order had already settled their admission. The difficult questions concerned the incident, its records, and real commercial consequences. She looked almost disappointed by the relief. Lin Yue understood why: an old error could become a habit of seeing every new page as the same crisis. Luo Shan gave her the corrected extract to read once more, then closed the unrelated city bundle before they resumed the present case.

court_cost_rubbed_seal.speaker: narrator
court_cost_rubbed_seal.text: One new seal smeared when Ru Fang lifted the comparison sheet too early. He set that copy aside as spoiled and made another under the same quoted fee. His error did not require a third four-copper charge. The spoiled page went into the clerk's recorded waste rather than back among the working exhibits. Dai checked its number against the replacement. Lin Yue had expected certification to look grander than this: a wet seal, a patient correction, and someone refusing to charge twice for finishing the job they had already agreed to perform.

court_cost_payment_order.speaker: narrator
court_cost_payment_order.text: Luo Shan prepared a payment order for the two completed extracts, but Ru Fang and the cashier checked it before release. His assistance signature confirmed the request, not the certification or the disbursement. The distinction slowed the task by several minutes. It also meant no one person could write a service into existence, declare it complete, and take the money. Ru Fang had to return to his own counter after signing. Luo Shan waited with the order instead of using his familiarity with the cashier to make the missing check seem unnecessary.

court_cost_ink_expense.speaker: narrator
court_cost_ink_expense.text: Dai wondered whether the extract price covered the extra ink used to preserve the correction history. Ru Fang pointed to the posted rate: the defined extract included ordinary materials and checking. If the offered scope had expanded into an entire book, the clerks would have needed a new quote before proceeding. It had not. Mei laughed softly at the question and then thanked Dai for asking it. Hidden small charges could become a barrier as surely as one large fare. The answer belonged on the worksheet, where another clerk would not have to ask it again.

court_cost_source_return.speaker: narrator
court_cost_source_return.text: The original keepers reviewed the return arrangements before leaving the comparison desk. Accepted copies could remain with the court under their offered use. Original books and slips would follow their separate custody terms. Payment for certification did not give the court a longer lease on everything a keeper brought into the room. Luo Shan placed the acknowledgments with the yellow access bundle and left the exhibits themselves where the custodian directed. Lin Yue was beginning to see the account as a map of bounded tasks. Each payment ended somewhere, even when a hearing's curiosity did not.

court_cost_du_message.speaker: narrator
court_cost_du_message.text: Du's second message arrived while the clerks put their seals away. He had understood the private preparation notice as compulsory and had considered borrowing the six copper from a neighbor. The correction reached him before he did. He asked whether declining the optional writer would leave his statement less complete. Luo Shan answered that appointed assistance remained available within the scheduled hour and that Du could submit an offered written supplement. He sent no bill with the answer. The six copper had never entered the access budget, but avoiding the unnecessary loan still mattered to someone below.

court_cost_jian_second_offer.speaker: narrator
court_cost_jian_second_offer.text: Jian returned with a different offer for anyone wanting private help beyond the court's appointed assistance. It listed the exact extra pages, price, and stopping time. Luo Shan read it without contempt. He himself earned part of his living from private petitions. The problem had been an unnecessary service dressed as a condition of admission, not the existence of paid writing. Dai kept the new offer at a separate desk. Lin Yue hoped the arrangement would survive a crowded morning, when people reached for the nearest packet and nobody had leisure to explain every sheet.

court_cost_working_copy.speaker: narrator
court_cost_working_copy.text: Lin Yue examined her working notes before leaving the copy desk. They contained her observations, not a third certified extract. She marked them accordingly. The court could hear an account of what she had seen, compare it with the certified pages, and ask her where she had misunderstood. She would not make her notebook more authoritative by adding a drawing of the seal. Outside the window, the rain briefly thinned enough to show the cliff path. Two travelers would soon use that path to offer evidence in forms more complicated than any copyer's tidy columns.

court_cost_storage_door.speaker: narrator
court_cost_storage_door.text: The storage door stood at the end of a short passage that smelled of oiled wood. Its custodian checked the accepted inventory before showing the room. One shelf held copies for the hearing; another held separately offered objects under their owners' terms. Blank spaces were marked for returns rather than future claims. The posted storage price was two copper per overnight interval for this defined case allocation. Six intervals would cost twelve. Lin Yue asked the custodian to write the first and last night plainly. The Day7 review date was longer than a careless reader might think that price covered.

court_cost_six_nights.speaker: narrator
court_cost_six_nights.text: Luo Shan numbered the storage intervals aloud. Arrival night, Day0. Then nights Day1, Day2, Day3, Day4, and Day5. Six nights ended with collection on the morning of Day6. The common hearing on Day3 fitted inside that period. The extension review on Day7 did not. Dai had first read through Day6 as though it bought the night after Day6 as well. The custodian corrected the wording before anyone paid. A calendar could hide an extra charge in a familiar phrase, particularly when an immortal court treated two nearby dates as nearly the same moment.

court_cost_storage_rate.speaker: narrator
court_cost_storage_rate.text: The two-copper rate covered the allocated dry shelf, routine custody entries, and the case's agreed protective wrapping. It did not buy unrestricted examination of the objects or repair damage already present when they arrived. The custodian showed the intake descriptions so those limits would be visible later. Lin Yue noticed a tear described in an offered packet's outer cloth. Its owner had accepted the cloth's condition and chosen a replacement wrapper. The new wrapper appeared on the routine supply account. Nobody had put the old tear into the accident file as though it were fresh damage from the court.

court_cost_owner_tags.speaker: narrator
court_cost_owner_tags.text: Each accepted object had two tags. One identified it for the hearing, and the other stated the keeper's custody terms. Lin Yue read the second tags first. A defined inspection did not automatically allow a destructive test, removal to another room, or retention past the agreed return. The custodian's storage price bought care within those terms. Luo Shan asked that the funded return date be written beside the custody deadline wherever they differed. A payment might expire before permission, or permission before payment. Neither difference could be repaired by pretending the tags meant the same thing.

court_cost_damp_packet.speaker: narrator
court_cost_damp_packet.text: A packet arriving from the lower landing had damp corners. The custodian paused intake rather than stacking it under a heavier box. Its keeper had permitted drying by ordinary air on a rack, with the contents still enclosed as agreed. Lin Yue helped clear the rack's surroundings without touching the packet. The drying space was already part of the quoted storage service. Rain could make a task inconvenient without creating a new fee. The custodian recorded the wet condition before drying, so the hearing would not mistake a later tidemark for evidence of a different journey.

court_cost_dry_rack.speaker: narrator
court_cost_dry_rack.text: The drying rack had no magical flame beneath it. It relied on space, moving air, and patient checks. Its oldest slat bowed slightly, leaving less room than the inventory diagram suggested. The custodian moved an empty tray rather than crowding the damp packet. Dai changed the diagram to match the room. Lin Yue had begun the inquiry expecting hidden levies and mysterious court debts. Some costs came from ordinary furniture that took up real space. If the final plan extended storage, it would have to reserve that space as well as provide copper for another line on the calendar.

court_cost_key_entry.speaker: narrator
court_cost_key_entry.text: The key book recorded who opened the room, when, and for which permitted task. Luo Shan's name appeared once for the inventory check, accompanied by the custodian's name. It did not grant him a standing right to enter while he drafted petitions. The ordinary court clerk could retrieve working copies from a different counter without opening the original-object shelf. Lin Yue copied that distinction into her notes. A final budget for specialist handling would need a task and an authorized custodian, rather than treating eight copper as a general invitation to explore every object behind a locked door.

court_cost_storage_choice.speaker: narrator
court_cost_storage_choice.text: Before the storage allocation was approved, the custodian offered three checks: compare the inventory with the owner's tags, verify the dry shelf and return schedule, or read the key entries for completed access tasks. All three would be done under the existing intake service. Lin Yue could join one and receive the other recorded results afterward. The custodian did not offer the objects for casual inspection while they chose. Even an inquiry about storage could become an excuse to handle more evidence than its owners had offered. Luo Shan kept the choice focused on care, timing, and authorized entries.

choices.text: Check the shelf and return calendar.

court_cost_tag_check.speaker: narrator
court_cost_tag_check.text: Lin Yue compared the accepted inventory with the owners' tags beside the custodian. One inventory line used a broad description that could include two separate pieces. Its owner's acknowledgment named only the offered outer fitting. The custodian narrowed the line and asked the keeper to confirm it before filing. No price changed. The correction reduced what the court appeared to hold. Lin Yue marked her own note as an inventory correction, not a discovery about the accident. A careful list could protect the offered evidence without turning the presence of an object into permission to investigate its entire history.

court_cost_shelf_check.speaker: narrator
court_cost_shelf_check.text: Lin Yue checked the reserved shelf's number against the return schedule. The space was free through the morning of Day6. Another case had requested it afterward, and the custodian would need a different available bay for any renewed storage. A fund reserve alone did not create that bay. Luo Shan sent a conditional inquiry rather than promising the shelf to two hearings. The custodian could hold an answer until the common Day3 decision. Its price would remain two copper per authorized overnight interval if a space was available. Lin Yue wrote the condition beside the sum.

court_cost_key_check.speaker: narrator
court_cost_key_check.text: Lin Yue read the key entries with Luo Shan. One access line ended without a closing time because the clerk had been interrupted by a messenger. The custodian checked the adjacent duty record and completed the entry with the clerk present, preserving the correction. It did not show an unexplained night visit or establish anyone's intent. Luo Shan asked why the first line had remained incomplete. The clerk answered plainly, and the answer joined the record. A small clerical error deserved repair at its own size rather than an accusation large enough to fill the whole hearing.

court_cost_storage_rejoin.speaker: narrator
court_cost_storage_rejoin.text: The inventory, shelf schedule, and key book checks returned without a new charge. One inventory description had narrowed, a possible extra bay remained conditional, and a missing closing time had been openly corrected. The baseline still bought six nights at two copper each. Luo Shan added twelve to the earlier fifty-two. Sixty-four copper now had defined uses. The remaining thirty-two lay untouched in the box. Dai wrote the Day6 collection time beneath the total and circled it. Whatever the common hearing chose, somebody would have to collect the exhibits or arrange separately permitted and funded care before that morning.

court_cost_return_carrier.speaker: narrator
court_cost_return_carrier.text: The custodian asked who would collect the originals at the end of the funded period. Some keepers intended to attend in person; others had specified authorized carriers. Lin Yue did not volunteer the Porcelain Courser merely because she knew an independent courier. That courier's city book permission was unrelated to a new court task. Luo Shan requested named return arrangements from the actual keepers. The question prevented a hidden assumption in the storage total. Twelve copper could buy six nights of care, but it did not buy someone else's labor to carry every item away afterward.

court_cost_custody_gap.speaker: narrator
court_cost_custody_gap.text: He Lian listened when Luo Shan described the interval between Day6 collection and Day7 review. She would not solve it by ordering originals to remain without their owners' terms. The common hearing could choose a bounded plan that paid for extra storage where available and sought the required permission. Otherwise, records would be used within their offered forms after originals returned. The magistrate asked that the gap appear on the public cost sheet. Lin Yue expected a grand legal formula. She gave them a date and a practical instruction: do not let uncertainty become unacknowledged custody.

court_cost_space_reply.speaker: narrator
court_cost_space_reply.text: The custodian's assistant answered about the extra bay. It could be reserved conditionally because another case's objects were scheduled for collection on Day5. Known changes would be reported before the Day3 hearing; later changes would be reported immediately. No objects would move into that bay before its vacancy was confirmed. Unavailable space would trigger the accepted fallback and release unused charges. An offered inspection's scope remained unchanged. Dai added those conditions to the reserve page. An apparently simple extension depended on other people finishing their own tasks.

court_cost_night_staff.speaker: narrator
court_cost_night_staff.text: Luo Shan asked whether extra storage nights would require another payment to the night custodian. The posted two-copper rate already included ordinary overnight custody for the agreed case allocation. No second attendant charge belonged on top of it. Specialist handling, if selected later, would pay for distinct limited tasks rather than ordinary keykeeping. The assistant answered from the rate book and let Luo Shan read the page. Dai copied the reference beneath the sum. The fund was still small, but its limit now followed services that could be described instead of fees appearing whenever someone asked a sensible question.

court_cost_daily_notice.speaker: narrator
court_cost_daily_notice.text: Dai placed a short notice outside the cost office: this case's baseline storage ended on the morning of Day6, and any later custody would require a separately authorized arrangement. She did not print the private exhibit list or its owners' addresses. A worker passing the door asked whether that meant the hearing ended on Day6. Luo Shan explained that the common hearing remained Day3 and the extension review Day7. The storage date belonged to one service, not the entire case. Dai returned to the notice and added those distinctions before another reader carried the misunderstanding downstairs.

court_cost_lunch_box.speaker: narrator
court_cost_lunch_box.text: Late afternoon, Luo Shan opened a lunch box that had gone cold during the inventory check. Dai offered to bring fresh tea from the staff kettle. Neither expense entered the ninety-six-copper account. Lin Yue ate beside them while the custodian locked the original-object shelf. For several minutes they discussed the crooked rack slat rather than the accident. Dai knew a carpenter who could replace it during the next ordinary maintenance day. The court would have to order that work from its own building account. A useful improvement did not become this case's cost merely because they had noticed the need.

court_cost_first_payment.speaker: narrator
court_cost_first_payment.text: The cashier released payment for the two completed extracts after checking their acknowledgments. Other baseline sums remained reserved until their services occurred. Eight copper had actually left the box; fifty-six more was allocated to specific future tasks; thirty-two remained uncommitted. Luo Shan wrote those three amounts separately. Dai's earlier worksheet had called every planned cost spent. Lin Yue preferred the new page. If weather canceled a journey, the court would need to know which money had been paid, which task remained possible, and which unused amount should return. A total could be correct while its verbs were wrong.

court_cost_accounts_board.speaker: narrator
court_cost_accounts_board.text: Lin Yue carried the corrected figures to the board beneath the invitations. The board displayed ninety-six authorized, sixty-four baseline allocated, and thirty-two uncommitted. Completed payments appeared in a smaller dated column. No one was promised the full fund simply by arriving first at the counter. Four attendance allocations were named, with private contact details omitted. A passerby asked why Du's injury did not earn him all the remaining copper. Luo Shan answered that this fund purchased access, while injury compensation and disputed responsibility required their own evidence and authority. The distinction could disappoint someone without making it optional.

court_cost_day1_bai.speaker: narrator
court_cost_day1_bai.text: Bai arrived on Day1 after the carrying-chair supervisor confirmed a safe covered-path journey. She rested before the statement hour and kept her own copy of the disputed assessment folded inside her sleeve. Luo Shan showed her the five-copper attendance term before beginning. It did not require an account favorable to the court or anyone else. Bai read the term, then asked whether her time at the stone yard would be paid separately. Luo Shan could not promise that from this fund. She nodded once, displeased but clear about the difference, and set her own work calendar on the table.

court_cost_bai_work.speaker: narrator
court_cost_bai_work.text: Bai's work calendar recorded stone deliveries and inspection appointments, with crossed-out tasks still visible. She had offered the relevant entries to the case under defined terms. The costs inquiry did not decide which entry established the disputed inspection. It recorded what the statement hour took from her day. Bai had arranged another stonebinder to finish one task and would owe that worker the agreed payment. Five copper covered the court's limited attendance allocation, not every consequence of leaving the yard. Lin Yue asked what a future invitation should say so a worker could calculate that difference before agreeing to come.

court_cost_bai_calendar.speaker: narrator
court_cost_bai_calendar.text: Bai wanted the invitation to name its stopping time before describing the seriousness of the court. Stone already cut for a delivery could not wait indefinitely on a narrow yard path. Her replacement worker needed to know whether she would be back to inspect the binding that evening. Luo Shan wrote that answer in the margin of his proposed future form. Bai was not asking the court to guarantee her whole income. She wanted to stop guessing how much of a working day a solemn phrase might consume. Dai asked permission to keep that practical sentence on the access worksheet.

court_cost_bai_receipt.speaker: narrator
court_cost_bai_receipt.text: The cashier prepared Bai's attendance receipt for five copper. It named the bounded statement appointment and contained no admission concerning the accident. Bai compared it with the separate acknowledgment for her offered calendar entries. She signed the payment receipt after the cashier read it aloud. Lin Yue watched her count the coins into a small cloth pocket. One roll of legal language could have made that modest payment feel like a bargain over her whole claim. Instead, she knew what it purchased: this appointment, completed on its own terms, while other questions remained open.

court_cost_bai_return.speaker: narrator
court_cost_bai_return.text: Bai's return began within the reserved carrying-chair service after the supervisor checked the path and her condition. She chose a short rest before entering the chair. The attendant helped only as agreed and kept the right side of the passage clear for other travelers. The closed goods lift remained closed. Dai marked the completed round trip and lower-landing assistance on their respective lines. Those services could now be paid without inventing another journey for Day3. Bai took her authorized statement copy below, where its useful words would have to share space with an unfinished evening's work.

court_cost_du_arrival.speaker: narrator
court_cost_du_arrival.text: Du arrived Day2 with his right shoulder supported and the stopping rules in effect. His clinician had permitted the seated transfer within stated limits, not declared him fit for ordinary lifting. He moved slowly from the carrying chair to the waiting bench. Luo Shan offered to postpone the statement if pain made the appointment unworkable. Du wanted to begin after resting, but asked for short questions. Lin Yue moved a heavy water jug before anyone asked Du to pour from it. The access plan would have failed quietly if they had overlooked that small task after paying for the journey.

court_cost_du_appointment.speaker: narrator
court_cost_du_appointment.text: Luo Shan said the five-copper attendance allocation did not depend on completing every later question. It covered the bounded appointment and could be recorded if his offered account had to stop early. The ordinary clerk would retain the authorized portion, and further questions could follow another permitted form. Du looked toward the door before answering. He had imagined being kept in the room until someone decided he sounded certain enough. Luo Shan showed him the stopping time. Du set his uninjured hand beside the page and began with the goods he had been carrying before the accident.

court_cost_du_household.speaker: narrator
court_cost_du_household.text: When the statement paused, Du explained why an indefinite court day frightened him. His household had divided chores around the injury, but nobody had gained more hours by dividing them. A neighbor had agreed to move two heavy jars that evening. Du still needed to prepare the lighter work he could manage. The five copper helped with one bounded attendance cost; it did not replace those tasks or settle his medical bill. Lin Yue put the distinction in her notes without publishing Du's household arrangements. The hearing needed the access constraint, not every private detail that made the constraint real.

court_cost_du_unpaid_work.speaker: narrator
court_cost_du_unpaid_work.text: Lin Yue asked how the disputed wage verification affected Du's immediate choices. Du had offered the relevant work entries to the court, and the corrected public proof was already admitted. The remaining claim could not be paid merely because the annex had used an improper temporary-license reference. Its actual work and amount still needed checking. Du understood that distinction. What he objected to was being told to wait as though waiting had no price. Luo Shan recorded the dated verification question for the docket inquiry rather than promising payment from the thirty-two copper reserved for access planning.

court_cost_time_choice.speaker: narrator
court_cost_time_choice.text: Luo Shan could clarify the attendance receipts, compare the scheduled hour with the invitation forms, or ask the cashier how an interrupted appointment was recorded. Lin Yue could join one of those checks while the other two were completed by the appointed staff. The choices would not change what Du was allowed to say about the accident. They concerned how the court paid for receiving it. Dai held up the old indefinite summons beside the new bounded invitation. It was easy to write until the court is satisfied. It was harder to decide what that phrase would cost another person.

court_cost_time_receipt.speaker: narrator
court_cost_time_receipt.text: Lin Yue compared the four attendance receipt forms. Each named five copper and its bounded testimony task. Bai and Du's receipts contained no release of damages claims. Sui's named off-shift explanation of his offered entries, distinct from ordinary lift duty. The Rain Heron's named a limited account paid through the agreed fish invoice, distinct from its seasonal inspection contract. The cashier removed a copied phrase about satisfaction of all obligations. That phrase belonged to a closed supplier bill, not these appointments. She preserved the correction before the remaining receipts were used.

court_cost_time_form.speaker: narrator
court_cost_time_form.text: Lin Yue checked the appointment forms with Dai. The new text named expected arrival, rest, statement length, and return service, with safety and clinician limits where needed. It still left room for a witness to stop or ask a question. Dai removed a decorative instruction to attend promptly at any hour the court might require. Luo Shan said that sentence had served a different kind of proceeding and did not belong in these invitations. The corrected forms would not make every future hearing affordable. They would at least reveal its demands before someone accepted a day they could not spare.

court_cost_time_interruption.speaker: narrator
court_cost_time_interruption.text: Lin Yue asked the cashier about an interrupted appointment. She pointed to the assistance order's attendance terms. The payment recognized reserved time and offered participation within the defined appointment; it was not a bounty for an uninterrupted recital. A witness who came and needed to stop would not owe the money back merely because the clerk wanted another answer. The appointment record would state what actually occurred. Luo Shan copied that rule onto the working sheet. The fund remained limited, but its limitation would not be enforced by pressuring a tired person to speak beyond the terms already agreed.

court_cost_time_rejoin.speaker: narrator
court_cost_time_rejoin.text: The receipt, invitation, and interruption checks reached the same conclusion. Four five-copper allocations paid four defined attendance tasks, not full lost income, favorable testimony, or unlimited availability. Staff corrected the language that had suggested otherwise before payment. Bai's completed receipt remained valid; Du could finish or stop under his appointment terms; Sui and the heron retained their separate ordinary work agreements. Lin Yue brought the summary to Luo Shan. The twenty-copper line on the budget had always added correctly. It had taken another hour to make its meaning as clear as its arithmetic.

court_cost_du_stop.speaker: narrator
court_cost_du_stop.text: Du ended his offered account before the scheduled hour because his right shoulder ached sharply. The clerk marked the stopping point and asked no final question disguised as a courtesy. Luo Shan reviewed the authorized portion with Du after a rest, without requiring another recital. The appointment receipt still named the agreed five copper. No one called the shorter statement a debt to the court. Lin Yue helped arrange the safe return within the carrying-chair reservation. Du's account would reach the common Day3 hearing as offered; its remaining questions would have to wait for another appropriate form.

court_cost_keeper_offshift.speaker: narrator
court_cost_keeper_offshift.text: Sui's attendance took place after his ordinary duty ended. He brought the offered log entries and identified which were his own work. The five-copper line covered that bounded explanation, not a promise that the entries settled causation. His employer's duty account still paid for ordinary maintenance, and the closed goods lift did not reopen because he had come to court. Luo Shan showed the cashier the end of Sui's shift before filing the attendance order. The separation mattered to Sui. He wanted to be paid for the additional hour without having his earlier work erased or charged twice.

court_cost_heron_receipt.speaker: narrator
court_cost_heron_receipt.text: The Rain Heron chose its agreed fish payment after completing the bounded account it had offered. The supplier acknowledged the five-copper invoice once. The service record also identified the separately agreed safe message flight and its stopping terms; no second five-copper allocation appeared. Seasonal inspections remained under the older agreement. Lin Yue asked whether the basket's empty reed lining belonged to the supplier. It did, and the supplier took it back. The bird moved to its offered resting perch while the clerk completed the record. Nobody could demand more testimony or another flight by pointing to that receipt.

court_cost_dai_break.speaker: narrator
court_cost_dai_break.text: Dai took her afternoon break after the attendance forms were corrected. She rubbed the cramped place between two fingers and admitted that she had copied much of the old worksheet because there were too many petitions to design each one anew. Luo Shan did not ask her to reinvent the court before tomorrow. He asked her to keep the corrected case sheet where the next clerk could find it. Lin Yue folded a clean cover around it. An improvement could last if someone had time to use it; otherwise, the older form would remain the easiest paper to reach.

court_cost_actual_paid.speaker: narrator
court_cost_actual_paid.text: Luo Shan reviewed the completed payments at the end of Day2. The two extracts had cost eight. The completed carrying-chair and assistance tasks would be paid against their receipts, within the planned twenty-four. Four bounded attendance allocations totaled twenty. Storage would be charged only for its agreed overnight intervals. Together, the baseline ceiling remained sixty-four. Some entries were completed and some still running; the uncommitted thirty-two remained separate. Lin Yue asked whether the court could spend that reserve tonight because the first tasks had gone well. Luo Shan shook his head. Success did not authorize an unrelated new purchase.

court_cost_private_bills.speaker: narrator
court_cost_private_bills.text: The private-bills bundle waited beneath the yellow access papers. It contained offered invoices whose relevance the merits inquiry would decide: treatment, work interruptions, repair labor, and other commercial claims. The costs route did not treat every invoice as established liability. It did confirm that a stayed assessment and suspended record-based work bar had not canceled genuine private obligations. Du's medical account continued under its own terms. Bai's hired replacement still expected agreed payment. Luo Shan drew a fresh boundary on the table. Access funding could make evidence reachable while leaving painful economic questions unresolved.

court_cost_clinician_note.speaker: narrator
court_cost_clinician_note.text: Du had permitted a short clinician's note about the journey limits, not the court's inspection of his entire treatment history. The note explained why seated travel, rest, and stopping rules mattered. A medical bill named treatment provided. Lin Yue did not copy its private details into the public cost sheet. The court could receive an appropriately offered bill in the relevant claim without publishing everything surrounding it. Luo Shan put the access note with the journey receipt and the offered billing material with the merits papers. Their shared handwriting did not make them the same evidence for the same purpose.

court_cost_stone_replacement.speaker: narrator
court_cost_stone_replacement.text: Bai's replacement worker sent a short acknowledgment of the Day1 stone-yard task. The promised payment belonged to their agreement, not the court's attendance allocation. Bai had offered the relevant acknowledgment as context for lost work, leaving unrelated yard customers outside it. Luo Shan recorded its source and limits for the hearing. He did not repay it from access money or declare that the accident assessment's payer must cover it. Lin Yue read the practical description of binding a delivery stack. Another worker had done real labor while Bai traveled, regardless of which account eventually proved her claim.

court_cost_repair_invoice.speaker: narrator
court_cost_repair_invoice.text: An offered repair invoice referred to work around the goods equipment. Its title sounded decisive, but Luo Shan asked the source keeper to distinguish proposed work, completed work, and payment already made. The costs inquiry would not decide which repair established the accident's cause or who owed the expense. It could prevent an estimate from being described as cash already spent. Lin Yue noted the invoice's verbs and sent that question to the maintenance inquiry. The closed goods lift still required the responsible safety staff's checks. A funding page could describe a repair without making the machine safe to use.

court_cost_supplier_memory.speaker: narrator
court_cost_supplier_memory.text: A supplier remembered giving a quote before the accident and completing a different delivery afterward. He permitted a comparison of those relevant entries, not the opening of his whole customer book. The papers had similar headings and different dates. Dai nearly stacked them together as duplicate copies until Luo Shan pointed out the distinction. Lin Yue placed a plain divider between them. The hearing might decide what either entry proved about maintenance or expense. For now, the costs inquiry made sure a quote and a delivery were not added as two payments for the same thing without checking their work.

court_cost_private_choice.speaker: narrator
court_cost_private_choice.text: Three private expense questions needed source clarification rather than a payment order. Lin Yue could join the check of proposed and completed repair work, review the access-only clinician note with Luo Shan, or compare Bai's replacement acknowledgment with her attendance receipt. The other inquiries would return their defined results. None could spend the thirty-two-copper reserve on private compensation. Luo Shan laid the papers far enough apart that one could be read without uncovering another. Lin Yue chose where her attention would help most, knowing that a clear expense was still different from a decided payer.

choices.text: Clarify proposed and completed repair work.
Distinguish yard work from court attendance.

court_cost_private_repair.speaker: narrator
court_cost_private_repair.text: Lin Yue joined the source comparison for repair costs. The offered quote listed proposed tasks, while the completion acknowledgment named the tasks performed. Where they differed, the source keeper preserved both rather than rewriting the older estimate. Luo Shan recorded that no access payment had funded either paper. Their significance for the new incident would be reported to the maintenance inquiry. Lin Yue left without a neat culprit or a bill she could settle. She had a narrower useful finding: these records described different stages of work and should not be totaled as though every figure were money already spent.

court_cost_private_clinician.speaker: narrator
court_cost_private_clinician.text: Lin Yue reviewed the access note beside Luo Shan. They copied only the offered travel limits needed for appointment planning and left the wider treatment material within its separate permission. The medical bill remained a claim for actual services under its own terms, with liability questions outside the access worksheet. Luo Shan corrected one heading that called all papers supporting attendance. A bill could support another claim without becoming a journey expense. Lin Yue watched him file the note where the carrying-chair supervisor could receive its permitted instructions without obtaining Du's private medical history.

court_cost_private_yard.speaker: narrator
court_cost_private_yard.text: Lin Yue compared the stone-yard acknowledgment with Bai's court attendance receipt. The worker's payment covered a yard task; the court's five copper covered a bounded appointment. Both could exist without being duplicate wages for the same work. Whether the private replacement expense belonged in a recoverable claim remained for the hearing's evidence and authority. Luo Shan marked that unresolved question plainly. Lin Yue thought of Dai's first worksheet, where anything called time had threatened to collapse into one line. Different people had done different labor. A correct total needed to keep their tasks visible.

court_cost_private_rejoin.speaker: narrator
court_cost_private_rejoin.text: The three checks returned without a new access expenditure. Repair records distinguished proposed from completed work. Du's access note remained separate from treatment billing. Bai's replacement acknowledgment remained separate from the court's attendance receipt. Luo Shan entered those findings as source and scope clarifications for the common hearing. The preliminary stay still protected against enforcing the disputed new assessment while evidence was gathered. It did not erase genuine private claims, reopen the closed goods lift, or decide who caused the accident. Lin Yue could now explain each boundary with an actual paper and task rather than a slogan.

court_cost_cashier_claim.speaker: narrator
court_cost_cashier_claim.text: The cashier received a request to take the remaining thirty-two copper as security for a private incident claim. She refused because the appropriation authorized hearing access, not collateral for liability still under review. The claimant's representative was entitled to submit the relevant claim through the proper docket. He was not entitled to seize a court assistance reserve by calling it available cash. Luo Shan recorded the refusal and its authority without describing the representative as dishonest. A visible sum attracted reasonable urgency as well as unreasonable shortcuts. The cashier needed an answer that would survive both.

court_cost_representative_reply.speaker: narrator
court_cost_representative_reply.text: The representative asked what help the court offered his client while the disputed assessment was stayed. Luo Shan pointed to the procedure for an offered claim, the current review date, and the ordinary assistance desk. He promised no priority borrowed from Bai's or Du's reservations. The representative left an authorized billing summary for the merits file. Lin Yue watched Dai add a receipt acknowledgment rather than a payment. Someone could deserve a timely answer without already having a proven right to this particular money. The court's task was to preserve that distinction while responding at a human pace.

court_cost_day2_evening.speaker: narrator
court_cost_day2_evening.text: By evening on Day2, the carrying-chair services had finished their booked tasks and the path supervisors had filed their receipts. Du was below, resting his right shoulder under his clinician's limits. Bai had returned to the yard. Neither would be required to climb again for the common Day3 hearing. Lin Yue stood beneath the terrace shelter and read their appointment records while rain tapped the outer gutter. The closed freight apparatus remained beyond a separate barrier. Access had been purchased along another route. She wanted tomorrow's cost summary to make that physical separation impossible to overlook.

court_cost_clerk_letter.speaker: narrator
court_cost_clerk_letter.text: Luo Shan wrote to the clerks preparing future invitations. He enclosed the corrected case worksheet and asked them to distinguish passengers, freight, ordinary staff work, private writing offers, and attendance tasks. Dai suggested an example for each line instead of another page of abstract instructions. Together they used this case's actual services and prices, with private details removed. The letter requested a form review through the court's ordinary administration. It did not spend the access reserve on redesigning the institution. Lin Yue checked the example dates, then left the staff to finish the work they were already paid to do.

court_cost_dai_private_work.speaker: narrator
court_cost_dai_private_work.text: Dai mentioned that she sometimes paid a private writer to arrange her own household petitions. She had clipped Jian's offer into the invitation because it resembled something she found useful. Luo Shan accepted that explanation without letting it stand as a defense of the unclear packet. Dai needed a way to offer extra help without making it look required. She chose a separate table and a plain notice describing appointed assistance first. The change cost no case money. It cost a little counter space and the willingness to move familiar papers from the easiest place to reach.

court_cost_shoulder_image.speaker: narrator
court_cost_shoulder_image.text: Lin Yue reread Du's stopped statement and remembered how slowly he had shifted his right arm on the bench. It would have been easy to make that image an argument for whichever financial plan Lin Yue preferred. She refused to write it that way. Pain explained an access limit; it did not prove the machine's cause, the inspection's timing, or a debt's amount. Luo Shan asked her to check whether the offered portion had been recorded accurately. Lin Yue did that smaller task. A vivid memory could sharpen attention while remaining a poor substitute for evidence it had never contained.

court_cost_bai_tool.speaker: narrator
court_cost_bai_tool.text: Bai had left a drawing of the tool she used for stonebinding inspection, within the account she offered. Lin Yue looked at the drawing's worn handle and precise dimensions. It made her work less abstract without proving that any disputed check had happened at the alleged time. Luo Shan filed it with her offered material under the clerk's instructions. The costs inquiry needed only her statement appointment and the real interruption to her day. The technical inquiry could ask the tool's relevant questions. Lin Yue resisted carrying an appealing detail from one inquiry into another merely because it seemed persuasive.

court_cost_private_notice.speaker: narrator
court_cost_private_notice.text: Dai drafted a public clarification about the fund. It named its hearing-access purpose, the sixty-four-copper baseline, and the thirty-two uncommitted reserve. It stated that other claims remained separately receivable and that the preliminary stay did not forgive established private obligations. Luo Shan shortened the language until a worker could read it while waiting at the counter. He left the review date visible rather than buried beneath clauses. Lin Yue pinned it beside the corrected storage notice. The board now admitted several unresolved things, which made it less comforting but more useful than its first handsome estimate.

court_cost_outstanding_supplier.speaker: narrator
court_cost_outstanding_supplier.text: The handcart keeper came for payment after both completed transfers. The cashier matched his two receipts with the travelers' accepted terms and released eight copper. He asked whether he should keep Day3 free for another court summons. Luo Shan said no additional transfer had been ordered or funded. If a later task was needed, the court would request a new quote and agreement. The keeper thanked him and accepted another customer's booking. Returning an unused claim on someone's time was part of closing the account, even when no coin was returned to the box.

court_cost_chair_payment.speaker: narrator
court_cost_chair_payment.text: The carrying-chair supervisor received sixteen copper for the two completed eight-copper round trips. The receipt described the covered footpath, safe rest stops, and supervised transfers. It did not name the closed counterweighted goods lift as a service provided. Dai compared that wording with her first worksheet and drew a clear correction through the old equipment category. Lin Yue kept the original page in the audit trail. The revised account showed a mistake repaired through an actually different service. It would have been less honest to erase the first line and leave readers wondering why the estimate had changed.

court_cost_completed_baseline.speaker: narrator
court_cost_completed_baseline.text: By the end of the second day, forty-four copper had paid completed journey and attendance tasks and eight had paid the two extracts. Twelve remained allocated to the six agreed storage nights as they occurred. Thirty-two remained uncommitted. Luo Shan totaled the categories again with the cashier present. Ninety-six still balanced. He wrote no surplus from imaginary canceled expenses because the journeys had happened and their suppliers had done the work. Lin Yue checked the date beside each completed line. A truthful balance kept both delivered services and unfinished obligations visible rather than reducing the case to one encouraging number.

court_cost_reserve_question.speaker: narrator
court_cost_reserve_question.text: He Lian asked what the thirty-two could accomplish before the Day7 review. Luo Shan had requested quotes for four bounded alternatives, each answering a different access difficulty. The magistrate wanted them compared after the independent inquiries reported, not chosen merely because one supplier arrived first. She could authorize one plan within the reserve and its permitted purpose. She could not multiply thirty-two into four equal promises. Lin Yue brought the empty comparison sheet to the witness room. Its columns would need dates, actual tasks, evidence limits, and what remained unresolved after the last copper was spent.

court_cost_plan_quotes.speaker: narrator
court_cost_plan_quotes.text: Four proposed service packets arrived before the common hearing. Each totaled thirty-two copper, but their matching totals concealed different work. One funded short weather observation, another two lower-landing testimony sessions, a third staged source checking and exhibit handling, and the fourth a limited dated remand with one reinspection. Luo Shan placed them around the reserve page without paying any deposit. Suppliers had offered conditional dates and terms, not guaranteed the case would end. Dai numbered the packets so the hearing could compare them without treating the first one on the table as already approved.

court_cost_weather_quote.speaker: narrator
court_cost_weather_quote.text: The weather proposal offered three independent observation shifts on Days3, Day4, and Day5 at six copper each. Eighteen. Instrument rental for those shifts cost six, dated public notices four, and storage for nights Day6 and Day7 four. Thirty-two together. The observer's work was distinct from ordinary lift safety duty and the Rain Heron's seasonal inspections. The report could describe local conditions and uncertainty, not certify what caused the accident two days before arrival. Luo Shan wrote that limit beside the price. Funding a useful measurement did not make it an answer to every question involving rain.

court_cost_observer_visit.speaker: narrator
court_cost_observer_visit.text: The proposed observer showed Lin Yue the instruments available for rent and a sample dated notice. The sample stated where a reading had been taken and when it would be superseded, leaving room for missing observations. The observer would work bounded shifts, not stand at the terrace through every hour of the forecast window. Eighteen copper paid those three shifts if authorized. Ordinary keepers would retain their safety duties. Lin Yue checked that the sample did not promise an open path or a closed canal on Day5. A measurement worth paying for could still be incomplete and uncertain.

court_cost_weather_storage.speaker: narrator
court_cost_weather_storage.text: Luo Shan checked the weather plan's four-copper storage line. It bought two additional nights, Day6 and Day7, where space and owner terms allowed. Custody authority after the Day7 review would have to be expressly renewed; payment alone could not supply that authority. If permission ended or the space was unavailable, unused storage money would return. Copies already offered could still support the review within their own terms. Dai wrote the conditions beneath the total rather than in a separate packet. The storage gap was a specific difficulty the plan addressed, with limits the hearing could actually see.

court_cost_local_quote.speaker: narrator
court_cost_local_quote.text: The local testimony proposal offered two optional sessions at the lower landing for twelve copper each. Each session paid a local minute-taker six, hired sheltered space two, and an attendant four. Twenty-four. A certified messenger service cost four; two extra storage nights cost another four. Thirty-two in all. No new Bai or Du ascent was required. The local minute-taker's task was separate from appointed court assistance and would record only what a participant offered. Luo Shan asked the supplier to name each session's length and stopping time before the hearing considered the quote.

court_cost_local_room.speaker: narrator
court_cost_local_room.text: The hired room belonged to a cooper who cleared a workbench for limited scheduled use. Two copper per session bought that sheltered space, not a permanent testimony office. The cooper would move his own tools beforehand and resume work afterward. Luo Shan requested a simple drawing showing the door, seats, and covered approach. A room that was cheap but unreachable would not solve the access problem. The drawing came back with a narrow threshold marked clearly. Lin Yue sent that detail to the witness inquiry rather than declaring the space suitable merely because its price fitted the reserve.

court_cost_local_writer.speaker: narrator
court_cost_local_writer.text: The proposed local minute-taker supplied a sample offered statement and correction acknowledgment. Six copper paid one bounded session's recording, readback, and defined return of the participant's copy. Ordinary court staff would later receive the authorized record under their existing duties. The local writer would not decide admissibility or turn a witness's uncertainty into confident prose. Luo Shan asked whether the quote included an interrupted session. It did, under its stated appointment terms. Lin Yue noticed that the careful attendance wording from the baseline could help here without charging the fund again for inventing the same rule.

court_cost_local_choice.speaker: narrator
court_cost_local_choice.text: The local proposal could be checked through its room access, its minute-taking terms, or its messenger's scope. Lin Yue would join one check while the other authorized inquiries supplied their findings. They were still comparing a proposal, not ordering the two sessions. A worker could decline to attend without surrendering already offered evidence or corrected public proofs. Luo Shan left blank spaces for the participants' separate choices. The matched thirty-two-copper total made the packet easy to compare with the weather plan, but it did not make the two kinds of work interchangeable.

court_cost_local_threshold.speaker: narrator
court_cost_local_threshold.text: Lin Yue examined the room drawing with the carrying-chair supervisor. A narrow threshold was not automatically impassable, but it needed a transfer arrangement and space to rest without blocking the door. The supervisor suggested a different seat placement within the hired room. The cooper accepted that arrangement for the quoted session price. The attendant's four copper covered the defined local access task, not general medical care. Lin Yue marked the change for witness review. No one asked Du to demonstrate the transfer for the sake of proving a sketch could work.

court_cost_local_readback.speaker: narrator
court_cost_local_readback.text: Lin Yue read the minute-taker's sample beside Luo Shan. It preserved the participant's corrections visibly and marked an unanswered question as unanswered. The hired task did not require every participant to agree on the inspection time. Luo Shan requested that the actual sessions use the same correction procedure, including stopping rules. The writer accepted within the six-copper price. Lin Yue folded the sample separately from the case's offered statements. A useful example belonged in the service proposal. It was not evidence that any new account would necessarily be complete or truthful.

court_cost_local_messenger.speaker: narrator
court_cost_local_messenger.text: Lin Yue reviewed the messenger service with Dai. Four copper covered the specified delivery of authorized session records along the available route, with an acknowledgment of receipt. It did not guarantee passage through unsafe weather or authorize the messenger to open private contents. A delayed delivery would carry its actual date rather than the date everyone hoped for. Luo Shan would include that condition in the hearing's comparison. A local session could spare an injured traveler a climb and still face ordinary transport uncertainty. The fund could pay for a defined attempt without buying impossible speed.

court_cost_local_rejoin.speaker: narrator
court_cost_local_rejoin.text: The local checks returned with a revised seat arrangement, clear correction and stopping terms, and a bounded messenger task. The quote remained twenty-four for two sessions, four for delivery, four for two extra storage nights. Thirty-two. The offered room's actual accessibility and each participant's agreement still needed confirmation before authorization. Luo Shan wrote those conditions beside the plan, leaving the proposal neither dismissed nor promised. Lin Yue compared it with the weather packet. One bought local opportunities to speak; the other bought short observations. Neither could fill the other's gaps simply because their totals matched.

court_cost_docket_quote.speaker: narrator
court_cost_docket_quote.text: The staged docket proposal used twelve copper for six source-checking hours at two each, eight for two specialist exhibit-handling tasks at four each, four for a messenger, and eight reserved for up to four additional storage nights. Thirty-two. The specialist work was distinct from ordinary staff copying and keykeeping. It would follow offered scopes, not take over whole books or reopen the goods equipment. Luo Shan wrote the possible nights as Day6 through Day9. Custody authority beyond the Day7 review would require express renewal, and unused money would return if those later nights were not permitted or needed.

court_cost_source_checker.speaker: narrator
court_cost_source_checker.text: The source checker listed six hours as a ceiling, not an estimate that could grow after appointment. Those hours would compare the offered log references and verification entries with authorized source acknowledgments. Any uncertainty left at the end would remain visible. Ordinary court clerks would retain their paid certification and docket duties. Luo Shan asked the checker to identify pauses caused by unavailable sources separately from completed work. The quote would pay actual bounded hours, with unused copper returned. Lin Yue liked the absence of a promise to reconcile each paper by working indefinitely until a neat answer emerged.

court_cost_handling_tasks.speaker: narrator
court_cost_handling_tasks.text: The exhibit specialist's two tasks involved safe placement of an offered fitting for the permitted comparison and its documented return to authorized custody. Each cost four copper within the quoted limits. The specialist would not test a closed mechanism, scrape a surface, or infer consent from a storage payment. The ordinary custodian would remain present where the owner's terms required it. Dai asked why normal keykeeping was insufficient. The specialist described the fitting's awkward weight and the support needed to move it without changing its condition. A defined physical skill, rather than an impressive title, explained the additional charge.

court_cost_docket_hours.speaker: narrator
court_cost_docket_hours.text: Lin Yue drew six small boxes beside the source-checking quote. Each box represented one paid hour, and none represented a whole day's availability. A separate record would identify the work actually completed in that hour. Luo Shan said the common hearing could choose priorities after all inquiries reported. The cost route should not rank the disputed sources before hearing their findings. Dai added a place for unfinished questions beneath the boxes. Staged checking might produce a dependable first comparison while leaving later tasks for a review. That limitation was part of the plan, not an embarrassment to hide.

court_cost_docket_storage.speaker: narrator
court_cost_docket_storage.text: Eight copper reserved up to four storage nights after the baseline collection point. The custodian could offer space conditionally, and owners' terms would govern each object separately. At Day7, the court would need renewed authority for anything kept longer. If renewal was refused, originals would return as agreed and unused storage money would be refunded. Accepted copies could continue under their offered terms. Luo Shan underlined reserved. The eight copper was a maximum commitment to a possible service, not a statement that every object would be detained until Day10 because the ledger had enough money.

court_cost_docket_notice.speaker: narrator
court_cost_docket_notice.text: The messenger's four-copper task would deliver the staged requests and source acknowledgments within their authorized scope. It did not pay for broad public accusations or repeated journeys whenever a clerk wanted another date checked. Luo Shan asked for a defined packet and return acknowledgment. The messenger accepted a delivery window subject to safe passage. Lin Yue wrote the same uncertainty beside the local testimony messenger line. The comparison sheet was becoming easier to read because similar services used similar verbs. It still showed different underlying work and different unanswered questions after each plan's finite ending.

court_cost_remand_quote.speaker: narrator
court_cost_remand_quote.text: The limited remand proposal used twelve copper for one independent lower-landing reinspection, six for dated notices and service, six for a certified supplemental extract, and eight for up to four additional storage nights. Thirty-two. The reinspection would occur only under physical safety restrictions and defined permission. It could not reopen the goods lift or decide liability by itself. The supplemental extract had a broader offered scope than either baseline excerpt and a separate six-copper quote. Luo Shan left that scope attached to the price so nobody would mistake a higher number for an unexplained surcharge.

court_cost_independent_quote.speaker: narrator
court_cost_independent_quote.text: The proposed independent inspector had not performed the disputed maintenance. Twelve copper covered one bounded visit, its defined observations, and a dated report of limits. The inspector would need safe access and the responsible staff's permission for any examination beyond the offered view. If conditions prevented the visit, the service terms required a new safe date or return of unused payment. Lin Yue asked whether the inspector could promise an answer about the original accident. The answer was no. A later examination could clarify conditions and records while leaving an earlier sequence contested.

court_cost_notice_service.speaker: narrator
court_cost_notice_service.text: Six copper covered the remand plan's dated notices and defined service to the relevant parties. The notice would state what had been ordered, what remained stayed, the physical restrictions still in force, and the Day7 review. It would not use a blank command to return whenever summoned. Luo Shan read the proposed service scope aloud to Dai. She removed an older heading that implied every private claim had been dismissed. The preliminary stay and limited remand were narrower. The extra clarity required ordinary staff attention, while the six-copper allocation paid the specified additional notice service.

court_cost_supplemental_extract.speaker: narrator
court_cost_supplemental_extract.text: Ru Fang reviewed the proposed supplemental extract's six-copper quote. Its offered scope required a longer comparison and defined related entries, unlike the two smaller baseline excerpts. The work would be certified by authorized clerks, with Luo Shan assisting only in the request. No payment had been ordered. The common hearing could decide whether that additional record was the useful next task after the other inquiries reported. Lin Yue attached the quote beside its scope rather than beneath a bare total. An unexplained price would have recreated the very confusion they had spent two days correcting.

court_cost_remand_storage.speaker: narrator
court_cost_remand_storage.text: The remand storage reserve followed the same rule as the staged docket plan: up to eight copper for nights Day6 through Day9, with actual space and owner terms, renewed authority at Day7, and unused sums returned. A remand could request another examination without granting possession of every original until it was finished. Luo Shan kept the distinction in the proposed order. Lin Yue imagined how easily a delay could become a quiet seizure when no one named the pickup date. This plan named it, along with the separate conditions that might permit a later date.

court_cost_plan_comparison.speaker: narrator
court_cost_plan_comparison.text: Lin Yue arranged the four thirty-two-copper proposals around the baseline sheet. Weather offered three observation shifts. Local sessions offered two bounded chances to speak without a court climb. Staged checking offered six paid comparison hours and defined handling. Remand offered one independent reinspection with notices and a supplemental extract. Each reserved finite storage under separate custody terms. All could leave important questions unanswered. The common hearing would need the witness, weather, and docket findings before choosing. Lin Yue wrote that dependence across the top of the page, making the costs packet a contribution rather than a decision disguised as arithmetic.

court_cost_reserve_choice.speaker: narrator
court_cost_reserve_choice.text: Luo Shan asked which proposal's conditions Lin Yue wanted to explain first in the costs report: short observation, local access, or staged records. The remaining plans would still appear with their complete quotes. This choice would shape the order of her account, not spend the reserve or settle the appeal. Dai had prepared a separate remand summary for every version of the packet. Lin Yue could emphasize a difficulty she understood while leaving the court room to choose differently after hearing the other teams. A clear report needed a beginning; a fair report also needed its other pages.

choices.text: Explain the short observation proposal first.

court_cost_emphasize_weather.speaker: narrator
court_cost_emphasize_weather.text: Lin Yue began her draft with the observation proposal. It purchased new bounded information before the forecast window, not certainty about the old accident. She listed eighteen for three shifts, six for instruments, four for dated notices, and four for two storage nights. Then she wrote what it would not purchase: continuous watching, safe passage, a guilt finding, or unlimited retention. Luo Shan placed the local, docket, and remand packets immediately behind the page. Lin Yue wanted the report's first emphasis to remain an emphasis, rather than becoming the only proposal another hurried reader noticed.

court_cost_emphasize_local.speaker: narrator
court_cost_emphasize_local.text: Lin Yue began her draft with the local sessions. She listed twenty-four for two twelve-copper appointments, four for the messenger, and four for two storage nights. The appointments would remain optional and separately offered, with no additional mandatory Bai or Du ascent. Their local records would not settle the accident simply because they were easier to obtain. Luo Shan placed the other three packets immediately behind the page. Lin Yue remembered Du's right shoulder and kept that memory out of the price column. It explained why access mattered without deciding which offered account the court should believe.

court_cost_emphasize_docket.speaker: narrator
court_cost_emphasize_docket.text: Lin Yue began her draft with the staged docket. She listed twelve for six source-checking hours, eight for two specialist tasks, four for the messenger, and eight reserved for up to four storage nights. Later custody required the Day7 renewal rather than an assumption drawn from paid space. Ordinary clerks' work remained on their own account. Luo Shan placed weather, local sessions, and remand behind the page. The neat sequence appealed to Lin Yue, but she left room for the other inquiries to show that a source or traveler could not fit the proposed order.

court_cost_reserve_rejoin.speaker: narrator
court_cost_reserve_rejoin.text: Whichever proposal opened the account, Luo Shan attached all four quotes and their limits. Thirty-two could fund one complete bounded plan, with unused sums returned where a service was not performed. It could not fund all four, guarantee conditions, or become private compensation. Dai checked the addition in each packet against the same reserve line. She found no arithmetic error and still read the conditions again. The morning's first worksheet had taught her that a page could add correctly while promising the wrong thing. The final report needed correct numbers joined to truthful verbs, dates, and tasks.

court_cost_hearing_order.speaker: narrator
court_cost_hearing_order.text: The ordinary clerk preparing the Day3 hearing asked how long the costs report would take. Luo Shan proposed a short account with the detailed sheets available for questions. No new attendance allocation was needed for his appointed court work or Lin Yue's voluntary report. The clerk placed costs after the independent factual summaries, so the financial alternatives could be understood in light of their actual constraints. Lin Yue agreed. An account that began with the cheapest plan before anyone explained the evidence might encourage the court to mistake saving money for resolving the case.

court_cost_dai_report.speaker: narrator
court_cost_dai_report.text: Dai wanted the original faulty estimate included rather than quietly replaced. It showed why the passenger category, appointment times, and optional writer notice had needed correction. Luo Shan warned that the hearing might ask her uncomfortable questions about it. She preferred those questions to leaving the next clerk an apparently perfect final page with no reason to understand its changes. Lin Yue placed the original and revised sheets together. Their difference was not a mystery about stolen coins. It was a sequence of ordinary assumptions that became costly when nobody checked the services those assumptions described.

court_cost_coin_count.speaker: narrator
court_cost_coin_count.text: The cashier counted the remaining physical rolls and matched them against paid receipts, running storage charges, and the uncommitted reserve. The ninety-six-copper authorization balanced without an unexplained missing amount. Lin Yue had expected the split cashbox corner to matter more. It was a repaired box, not evidence of theft. She left the repair out of her conclusions. Luo Shan kept the dated count acknowledgment in the administrative bundle. The hearing could see that the fund existed and had bounded uses without being distracted by a dramatic story its wooden container had never supported.

court_cost_supplier_confirmations.speaker: narrator
court_cost_supplier_confirmations.text: Before the report left the office, suppliers confirmed the conditional proposal dates and prices. Confirmation did not amount to authorization. No one should turn away paid work indefinitely because the court was considering a plan. Luo Shan stated when the common hearing would answer and what happened if the offer expired first. A later quote could differ. Dai added that practical deadline to each proposal packet. Lin Yue appreciated the small fairness of returning uncertainty to the institution that created it instead of letting every supplier carry the uncertainty unpaid while the court took its time.

court_cost_owners_reply.speaker: narrator
court_cost_owners_reply.text: Replies from exhibit keepers clarified which storage extensions they might permit and which originals had to return sooner. Luo Shan attached each reply to its relevant inventory line without forcing one common deadline onto all objects. A proposed extra bay could hold only items whose terms allowed it. Copies might remain usable when an original returned. The final plan could therefore spend less than its storage ceiling. Lin Yue checked that unused sums would be returned rather than moved silently into another task. An owner declining longer custody was not creating a debt to the court's chosen budget.

court_cost_day3_morning.speaker: narrator
court_cost_day3_morning.text: On the morning of Day3, Lin Yue walked the covered approach above the closed goods equipment. The carrying-chair supervisor was preparing an unrelated customer's safe journey under a new booking. Bai and Du were below with their authorized statements already before the court. The Rain Heron stood on its resting perch between ordinary duties. Lin Yue carried the costs packet past the barrier without stopping to inspect anything. Today's hearing would gather different inquiries into one record. She wanted each record to keep its own source clear when the room began making arguments larger than any single observer could support.

court_cost_bai_followup.speaker: narrator
court_cost_bai_followup.text: Bai sent a follow-up note before the hearing. She wanted the cost sheet to show that accepting five copper had not settled her disputed assessment or paid her replacement worker. The receipt already said that, but Luo Shan acknowledged the concern and attached the clarification to her offered material. He did not require her to travel again to restate it. Lin Yue thought of how a small payment could become a large rumor after it left the cashier's desk. The account needed wording strong enough to remain clear when repeated by someone who had not watched the coins change hands.

court_cost_du_followup.speaker: narrator
court_cost_du_followup.text: Du's follow-up confirmed his stopped statement's portion authorized for hearing. It repeated that his right shoulder's limits remained and that he had not accepted ordinary lifting work merely by making the seated journey. The costs packet would not decide his work capacity. Its completed transport receipt described the service actually used and the appointment that ended early. Luo Shan placed the follow-up with Du's account rather than rewriting the receipt into a medical conclusion. Lin Yue was glad the court could receive this clarification without asking an injured man to prove his discomfort on its stairs again.

court_cost_luo_private_deadline.speaker: narrator
court_cost_luo_private_deadline.text: Luo Shan's private merchant petition was a day late under his rescheduled agreement. He had not charged its lost fee to the hearing access fund. The merchant had accepted a new appointment and a smaller scope; another writer would take the remaining work. Luo Shan told Lin Yue this while packing the court papers, without asking for sympathy.
