His appointed hours had a cost outside the case, but that did not turn every consequence into a permitted expense. Lin Yue helped tie the bundle. The account's limits mattered most when someone who understood them still wished for more money.

court_cost_staff_capacity.speaker: narrator
court_cost_staff_capacity.text: Dai asked whether every future hearing could receive this many checks. Luo Shan said the ordinary administration would need to review staffing rather than pretend the corrected form supplied extra hands. Their case report could identify the work required and the errors caught. It could not promise that clerks would always have spare time. Lin Yue wrote a short administrative recommendation separate from the thirty-two-copper proposals. Its words would not count as another funded service. The court would have to decide later how to maintain useful procedures without making exhausted staff copy the old shortcuts again.

court_cost_final_sheet.speaker: narrator
court_cost_final_sheet.text: The final baseline sheet named sixteen copper for two assisted carrying-chair round trips, eight for two lower-landing transfers, twenty for four bounded attendance tasks, eight for two certified extracts, and twelve for six storage nights. Sixty-four. The authorization was ninety-six, leaving thirty-two for one mutually exclusive proposal. Lin Yue read the services rather than merely reciting the total. The closed goods lift appeared only as a separate safety restriction and incident source. No access payment reopened it. Day6 collection, Day7 review, and the conditional extra storage terms remained visible on the same page.

court_cost_remaining_needs.speaker: narrator
court_cost_remaining_needs.text: Luo Shan listed needs the fund would leave unmet. It did not replace full lost wages, pay every treatment expense, settle private liability, promise more than the bounded appointments, or fund an endless weather station. Some useful sources might remain unavailable at the review. Some service dates might change with safe passage. The court could still make a timely limited order based on authorized findings. Lin Yue placed that list before the detailed proposals, where a reader would encounter the shortages as part of the decision rather than discovering them later beneath the optimism of a completed payment.

court_cost_no_loan.speaker: narrator
court_cost_no_loan.text: A clerk suggested borrowing against next month's assistance appropriation if the hearing wanted both weather observation and local sessions. The cashier had no authority to make that promise. Other petitioners would need next month's fund, and its balance had not been allocated. He Lian could request a new appropriation through the proper process, with its own answer and delay, but today's choices had ninety-six existing copper. Luo Shan struck the imagined loan from the comparison margin. Lin Yue preferred the painful choice between real tasks to a generous promise whose payer would arrive later carrying someone else's unmet petition.

court_cost_copy_for_board.speaker: narrator
court_cost_copy_for_board.text: Dai prepared a public version of the cost sheet under her staff duties. It preserved totals, services, dates, and conditions while excluding private addresses, medical details, and unrelated customer names. The full authorized administrative packet remained available through the proper court process. She checked the public version against it line by line. Lin Yue pointed out one missing cancellation term, and she restored it. The board would help people understand what the court had bought without making the privacy of an offered record part of the price. Publication was another task with boundaries worth stating before the page went outside.

court_cost_report_choice.speaker: narrator
court_cost_report_choice.text: Lin Yue could open her short hearing account with the corrected access total or with the Day6 storage gap. Both belonged in every version, followed by the four unspent proposals and their limits. Luo Shan would answer the staff-service questions, and the authorized clerks would support their own certifications. Lin Yue would speak only for the checks she had joined and the reported administrative results whose sources were identified. Choosing an opening might help the court understand a difficult packet. It would not authorize her to announce what the other independent inquiries had found before their authors presented it.

choices.text: Open with the corrected access total.
Open with the storage calendar gap.

court_cost_report_total.speaker: narrator
court_cost_report_total.text: Lin Yue's written opening named the ninety-six-copper authorization and sixty-four-copper baseline. She listed each service, its date, and its completed or continuing status before explaining the thirty-two uncommitted reserve. The arithmetic would give the common hearing a stable start after the independent factual summaries. Then her draft described unpurchased needs and Day6 collection before the Day7 review. Luo Shan kept the detailed sheets beside her for checking. Lin Yue recommended no final plan yet. A clear opening should make the evidence easier to assess, rather than hurry the court toward whichever proposal had the neatest sum.

court_cost_report_gap.speaker: narrator
court_cost_report_gap.text: Lin Yue's alternative written opening named Day6 collection and Day7 review. That mismatch would draw attention to the calendar before prices. Her draft then explained ninety-six authorized copper, sixty-four baseline allocation, and thirty-two uncommitted. Four proposals offered different bounded next tasks with finite storage and explicit custody terms. None could solve every need. Luo Shan kept the original and corrected estimates ready for checking. The actual account would follow the independent factual summaries at the common hearing. Its opening order remained flexible; urgency about storage could not authorize spending before the whole record showed which work was useful.

court_cost_findings_packet.speaker: narrator
court_cost_findings_packet.text: Luo Shan delivered the administrative packet to the ordinary clerk. It contained the original estimate, corrected baseline, completed receipts, running storage terms, clarified optional writer notice, four conditional thirty-two-copper quotes, and authorized source acknowledgments. The clerk recorded receipt without treating that act as a merits ruling. Lin Yue identified the inquiries she had personally joined and the named staff results she had received. Bai's and Du's statements remained their offered accounts. The payment records did not prove the accident's cause. The court now had an exact account of access costs to place beside the other teams' evidence.

court_cost_departure.speaker: narrator
court_cost_departure.text: Lin Yue returned to the investigators' bench while Luo Shan took his place near the clerk. Dai stood by the cost packet, ready to explain her original assumptions and their corrections. The cashbox stayed in the office with thirty-two still uncommitted. Beyond the hall's open edge, rain hid part of the lower path. The hearing would have to choose its next bounded work under that uncertainty, after every authorized team reported. Lin Yue set down her notebook. She had brought money into clearer relation with labor and time; the difficult questions about the accident still awaited the whole record.

court_docket_entry.speaker: narrator
court_docket_entry.text: The docket room occupied the oldest wing. A brass gutter crossed its ceiling and descended beside the clerk's desk. For each accepted packet, the clerk opened a small tap; one measured trickle tipped a balanced spoon into a basin. The clerk paired that tip with the written intake entry. Luo Shan put the city packet on the dry side and asked Lin Yue to watch. This signal marked desk acceptance, not the earlier request below. Across the wall, forty drawers read awaiting a complete appearance, their handles polished by frequent touching.

court_docket_threshold.speaker: luo_shan
court_docket_threshold.text: A petition has three moments here: when someone first asks, when a clerk accepts the materials, and when the court considers the file complete. These used to be separate columns. The present cover gives you one date, whichever clerk last prepared it. Before we discuss the exchange's appeal, I want that distinction restored in our working notes. A person can answer promptly and still wait inside a drawer. We must also avoid calling every unfinished file a refused hearing. Some remain unfinished because the applicant chose to gather another piece of evidence.

court_docket_worktable.speaker: narrator
court_docket_worktable.text: Luo Shan borrowed a table whose legs were unequal. Shen Qing folded a waste envelope under the short one, then removed it when the keeper brought a wooden wedge. The keeper needed the envelope for comparing the court's older folds. This small correction made their preparation slower and rather more useful. They spread clean paper over the repaired table, leaving space for three source columns. Lin Yue placed the city hearing copy in its own wrapper. Nothing from the exchange became a court exhibit merely by sharing this room with an official seal.

court_docket_living_queue.speaker: lin_yue
court_docket_living_queue.text: I counted eleven people on the lower stair, although the docket board lists four visitors today. The keeper says several are accompanying applicants, and two came only to ask about a future date. We should learn which inconvenience belongs to which process before putting that count in a report. Still, the board describes a quieter room than the one below it. Can we begin with the people willing to explain that difference? If somebody wants only directions, our investigation must not turn their visit into testimony or require them to tell us their business.

court_docket_petitioner.speaker: narrator
court_docket_petitioner.text: The first willing visitor was Deng Yuan, a sixty-three-year-old maker of roof tiles. He had come to correct the recorded quantity of a kiln delivery, with the buyer's acknowledgment folded inside his sleeve. The quantity dispute was small; a difference of eighteen tiles mattered enough to him. His difficulty lay in the court's request that he attend three successive dry evenings before the file could be certified. Those evenings overlapped his only kiln firing that month. He offered the scheduling notice for inspection and kept the buyer's acknowledgment covered until its owner could answer.

court_docket_roofmaker_terms.speaker: luo_shan
court_docket_roofmaker_terms.text: Deng Yuan is not offering his entire trade book. He allows us to copy the scheduling sentence, his application dates, and the keeper's initials on this notice. The buyer's acknowledgment remains outside our packet unless separate permission follows. We can record that such a document exists without describing its contents as established evidence. He wants a workable opportunity to present the tile claim. He has not asked us to settle it from this stair, and he has not promised to abandon the firing. Please leave room for those limits beside his name.

court_docket_first_dates.speaker: narrator
court_docket_first_dates.text: Deng's notice contained two dates a week apart. The earlier appeared beneath a crowded stamp, and the later sat neatly inside the box marked appearance received. Luo Shan copied both while Deng held the original by its corners. A narrow grease mark crossed the earlier ink. He explained that he had carried the notice to the kiln before bringing it back to the court. No one could infer the earlier stamp's meaning from that stain. Shen Qing asked for the office's stamping guide, and the keeper fetched a booklet with several amendments sewn into its spine.

court_docket_stamping_guide.speaker: shen_qing
court_docket_stamping_guide.text: The earlier mark means a request for a visit, according to the amendment used this spring. The later box means receipt of the applicant's material. Neither says the file was judged complete. I am copying the guide's wording beside the notice, with the page number and amendment date. If a different clerk used an older rule, we will need that clerk's account rather than an argument from the mark alone. The grease obscures one initial, so that person remains unidentified for now. Our clean copy should retain the uncertainty instead of supplying a convenient letter.

court_docket_queue_table.speaker: narrator
court_docket_queue_table.text: The keeper produced a daily table showing four accepted appearances. Beneath it, an unheaded scratch sheet counted visitors sent away to return with dry papers. Two tallies matched Deng's earlier dates. Another referred to a person who never entered the room. Luo Shan asked the keeper to identify what he remembered personally. He remembered receiving the scratch sheet from yesterday's assistant and copying its totals; he had not witnessed its individual refusals. They labeled his account as a description of office practice, leaving the events themselves open for the assistant to confirm.

court_docket_keeper_limit.speaker: he_lian
court_docket_keeper_limit.text: The keeper can tell us how this room works and what he did within it. His copied total does not become eleven independent recollections. Keep the table and scratch sheet together, but do not merge their authors. I have used these summaries for many years, often when reviewing an absent colleague's work. That habit may have concealed differences which matter here. It gives us a reason to investigate, not a conclusion about every file in the drawers. Ask the assistant whether she is willing to explain the visits she actually handled.

court_docket_scope_map.speaker: narrator
court_docket_scope_map.text: They drew a map of offices rather than an accusation. The stair keeper controlled invitations and the handling of wet papers. The docket clerk classified a received packet as complete or incomplete. He Lian could order a hearing and review a classification within the court's jurisdiction. The city registrar retained authority over the public proofs already restored below. The exchange's commercial claims traveled in another column. Lin Yue marked several connecting arrows with question marks. The assistant had not yet explained whether those arrows described a rule, a shortcut, or a mistaken instruction.

court_docket_first_choice.speaker: lin_yue
court_docket_first_choice.text: We can begin with the office's written rules, the assistant's own handling of Deng's visits, or the route by which wet papers reach this desk. Each question might clarify a different part of the same delay. Luo Shan has asked another pair of clerks to preserve the sources we do not inspect ourselves, so nobody should describe their findings as something we watched. I want a first step narrow enough that its answer changes our next question. Deng still needs to return to his kiln; our method must leave him a usable departure time.

court_docket_rules_path.speaker: shen_qing
court_docket_rules_path.text: The rule booklet's earliest instruction requires a stable record of the offered statement. A later note recommends three dry evenings when water has damaged the paper. The newest desk card repeats the recommendation without the condition that made it useful. I have copied all three, because a shortened instruction can look older than the qualification it lost. We should ask who approved the desk card and whether clerks were told to apply it to dry originals too. The booklet alone does not establish how Deng's undamaged notice was handled on either visit.

court_docket_assistant_path.speaker: narrator
court_docket_assistant_path.text: The assistant, a forty-seven-year-old woman named Cai Fen, remembered Deng's first visit because his kiln apron shed pale dust across the stair. She had pointed him toward the three-evening card after checking that his sleeve was dry. She had not examined the covered acknowledgment. Cai offered her own account and the time tally she kept for staffing, with unrelated visitors' names concealed. She had followed the desk card as an ordinary requirement. When Luo Shan showed her the longer condition, she asked whether the office would correct its public directions before the next queue formed.

court_docket_paper_path.speaker: narrator
court_docket_paper_path.text: The keeper carried a sample folded petition from the terrace to the receiving shelf. A roof channel sheltered most of the walk, but the last turn passed under a broken joint. He ordinarily tucked papers beneath his coat there. On busy days the assistant moved them in an open tray, following an older instruction to keep each visitor's bundle visible. The sample acquired three drops before reaching the shelf. Lin Yue recorded the route and its present condition. They had demonstrated a risk of damage, not proved that every damaged petition came through this particular joint.

court_docket_first_rejoin.speaker: luo_shan
court_docket_first_rejoin.text: We have three findings to preserve separately: a shortened instruction, an assistant's account of following it, and a transfer route which can wet an otherwise dry paper. The other clerks have supplied signed notes for the parts we did not personally inspect. None identifies a person who deliberately delayed Deng. All three explain why merely asking him to try again may reproduce the problem. He has agreed to let us carry his scheduling question, and he leaves now with a receipt for the copied passages. His tile quantity remains undecided, where it belongs.

court_docket_departing_deng.speaker: narrator
court_docket_departing_deng.text: Deng read the receipt twice, once for the copied passages and again for the return date left blank. Luo Shan explained that a blank was not a promise of an immediate hearing. It meant the investigation had not selected a date on his behalf. He took a spare cover for the kiln acknowledgment and declined an escort because he knew the lower steps well. Below the court, the rain thinned into a silver curtain. His departure freed a place on the stair but did not reduce the number of unfinished files waiting behind the brass gutter.

court_docket_authority_question.speaker: lin_yue
court_docket_authority_question.text: Which officer can replace the shortened instruction today, and which officer can change the three-evening practice itself? Those sound like the same task until somebody discovers a charter clause behind the practice. I would rather find the distinction while Cai Fen is available to explain her desk work. If she receives another card tonight, she should know whether it corrects a copying error or announces a new rule. We also need to tell the people below what remains unchanged, including their right to bring ordinary evidence and the uncertainty of the eventual tile judgment.

court_docket_two_authorities.speaker: he_lian
court_docket_two_authorities.text: I can direct the keeper to display the full existing instruction and stop treating its recommendation as universal. A standing rule that genuinely requires repeated appearances would need the court's formal review, with notice to those relying on it. We must establish whether such a rule was ever adopted. My memory of its use is not enough. For now, preserve both cards and show the complete wording beside the shortened one. That makes the present directions intelligible without pretending this branch has resolved every disputed classification or approved a new way of taking evidence.

court_docket_notice_copy.speaker: narrator
court_docket_notice_copy.text: Cai Fen wrote the complete instruction on fresh paper while the keeper retained the shortened card in a dated cover. He Lian signed a direction identifying the old condition and the temporary display correction. It did not grant a hearing to any named applicant. Shen Qing watched the new paper placed low enough for a person seated on the stair to read. A visitor asked whether three evenings were still required. Cai answered by reading the condition aloud, then asked what condition his own notice described. The queue acquired a question it could actually answer.

court_docket_institution_memory.speaker: elder_yun
court_docket_institution_memory.text: I recognize the comfort of a desk card. One clear sentence seems kinder than an old booklet with its additions, and then a season passes before anyone notices what the sentence omitted. The consequence is real even when its maker meant to simplify work. Our report should examine who was able to check the card, who was expected to use it, and who paid for its defect. We must preserve Cai's account without making her the sole author of an instruction she received. He Lian's long use of the summary belongs in that account too.

court_docket_act_one_close.speaker: narrator
court_docket_act_one_close.text: The gutter tipped another spoonful while Luo Shan filed the corrected display direction beside the original notice. Their working map now had one solid arrow: the judge could correct the posted wording of an existing instruction. Several other arrows stayed uncertain. A drawer label offered only the date on which a file became complete, leaving earlier requests invisible. They would next examine how that label had been introduced, who supplied the completion date, and whether applicants could contest it. Through the wall came the keeper's patient repetition of the newly restored condition.

court_docket_landing_packet.speaker: narrator
court_docket_landing_packet.text: On their return to the table, Luo Shan opened the wrapper marked lower landing. Its cover already carried the emergency receipt granted that morning. Seven days for gathering evidence, a suspended disputed civil assessment, and a suspended record-based work bar were written beneath the accepted work proof. The receipt left physical safety restrictions and genuine private claims in place. Lin Yue copied those distinctions at the top of their comparison sheet. Nothing discovered about the filing could quietly erase the protection while the inquiry continued, and nothing in that protection had decided why the sling slipped.

court_docket_case_dates.speaker: luo_shan
court_docket_case_dates.text: The accident was reported as occurring two days before our arrival, around the third market bell. Du Heng is thirty-one and has an injured right shoulder. Bai Qun is forty-four and works as a stonebinder with a daily landing and guide-inspection remit. These are our starting descriptions, not a finding that either person caused the accident. The written reports contain claims about the sling and safety rope that still need comparison. Keep the market bell named in the chronology. A court bell on a separate mechanism cannot silently take its place.

court_docket_request_and_report.speaker: narrator
court_docket_request_and_report.text: The first petition asked for maintenance information, payment for interrupted work, and a hearing of the disputed responsibility assessment. A separate accident report summarized the injured porter's account. The two papers had been placed under one fastening, encouraging readers to treat their sentences as a single statement. Luo Shan removed only the outer fastening, with the keeper watching, and gave each sheet its own working label. The request showed what the applicants wanted considered. The report showed what its writer had been told. Neither document could make the other a witnessed account merely by being filed beside it.

court_docket_valid_proof.speaker: lin_yue
court_docket_valid_proof.text: Du's corrected city work proof was admitted before this investigation began. We are examining what work he was authorized to perform and what this filing claimed about that work, not asking him to earn his public identity again. The city correction remains effective whichever reform its hearing selected. I want a separate heading for scope so a disagreement there cannot drift into another hold on his name. He may still face genuine commercial questions. Those must be described as particular claims, with their own basis, rather than as a reason to withdraw his valid proof.

court_docket_annex_title.speaker: narrator
court_docket_annex_title.text: The annex bore a confident title: corroboration of work authority. Its first column repeated a temporary-license classification from the city exchange's older paperwork. Another column extended the classification into a description of responsibility at the landing. The copied heading made this look like a second source confirming the petition's account. Shen Qing placed the admitted city judgment beside it. That judgment preserved a correction history and distinguished licensed exterior recognition from the worker's own proof. The annex retained the old label without that history. Its neatness was a property of copying, not of accuracy.

court_docket_city_source.speaker: mei_dulan
court_docket_city_source.text: The enclosed judgment copy identifies the public correction and the limits of our decision. A temporary recognition-use license does not transfer its wearer's name, memory, or all duties attached to a job. The old exchange classification cannot extend a landing guide's contract either. I can explain the city records under my care and verify the authorized extract. I cannot certify the court's understanding of landing equipment. If its annex drew conclusions beyond our judgment, preserve that annex alongside the source and ask its own author to explain the step. Correcting our copy alone would leave the court's claim unexplained.

court_docket_copy_chain.speaker: narrator
court_docket_copy_chain.text: Mei's explanation arrived with the authorized city extract and a note identifying its source pages. Luo Shan laid out the chain in four positions: the original temporary rental record, the city hearing's correction, the court's shortened annex, and the filing index that cited the annex. Only the last two belonged to the court's handling of this petition. Some phrases repeated exactly across all four positions while their qualifications changed. Lin Yue drew a line around each repeated phrase rather than treating every appearance as corroboration. The chain could preserve a mistake as efficiently as it preserved a correct date.

court_docket_index_columns.speaker: shen_qing
court_docket_index_columns.text: The index lists the petition, the accident report, and the authority annex as three supporting documents. That is an inventory, not a count of independent witnesses. One description says confirmed by records, without naming which statement was confirmed. I am leaving the inventory intact and adding a comparison column in our notes. We can identify common sources without destroying the court's first record of what it received. If the description later changes, the dated amendment should say why. A clean replacement that makes the old wording vanish would prevent us from understanding who relied on it.

court_docket_classification_door.speaker: narrator
court_docket_classification_door.text: At the classification desk, an assistant pulled a wooden shutter across the room's smallest window to keep wind from lifting the pages. The closed shutter left the desk card difficult to read from the corridor. He explained that an incomplete authority annex ordinarily sent a case into the seventy-five-day verification cycle. This landing petition had received emergency protection instead of waiting unprotected. Its unresolved evidence still remained in the ordinary classification queue. Luo Shan asked for the rule behind that queue and the dated decision applying it, not merely another description of how the desk usually worked.

court_docket_source_choice.speaker: lin_yue
court_docket_source_choice.text: The copied words have traveled through several hands, and the next question depends on which gap we examine first. We can compare the city judgment's qualifications, ask the annex writer what she was trying to certify, or reconstruct how the index drew its supporting-document count. The other clerks will preserve the remaining two inquiries as signed source notes. Whichever road we take, a later answer must distinguish what we observed from what another team supplied. The emergency receipt stays visible on the table while we work, so the accepted proof cannot disappear beneath our comparisons.

court_docket_judgment_path.speaker: narrator
court_docket_judgment_path.text: Mei unfolded the correction warrant beneath a weighted glass corner. The original rental term authorized temporary public recognition for specified work. The correction restored public proofs and proper wage-account claims without deciding every return price. She pointed to the retained old entry, marked as corrected rather than scraped away. The court annex's phrasing came from that old entry, while the extract accompanying this packet showed its correction. Lin Yue recorded the mismatch and Mei's source limits. The city had supplied both pieces; someone at the court had chosen a shorter account of them.

court_docket_writer_path.speaker: narrator
court_docket_writer_path.text: The annex writer, a fifty-six-year-old clerk named Rui Fang, offered her marked draft. Her instruction had been to identify the documents showing lawful work, and she had copied the first recognizable license heading before reading the correction. A supervisor had added the word corroboration during review. Rui retained both handwriting changes on the draft. She accepted that the completed annex omitted a relevant qualification. She did not claim to know whether that omission changed the later assessment. That question required the assessing office's own account, not an inference from her embarrassment at the table.

court_docket_index_path.speaker: narrator
court_docket_index_path.text: The index keeper showed the stamp used for supporting documents. It counted separate sheets after they were folded and fastened, including copied extracts. The stamp's small boxes had no place to distinguish a copied statement from a fresh observation. He had put three marks on the landing cover because three document types arrived. Another clerk later read those marks as three confirmations. Luo Shan copied the keeper's explanation beside a sample stamp and asked the later reader to identify the sentence she had understood as confirmed. The stamp itself could not answer that question.

court_docket_source_rejoin.speaker: luo_shan
court_docket_source_rejoin.text: The retained judgment establishes that Du's corrected proof remains valid. The annex draft identifies an omitted qualification and a supervisor's added description. The index method counts sheets, leaving independence unstated. We have signed notes for each finding, including the parts another team examined. These sources explain a route by which a classification could become overstated. They do not prove which individual conclusion the assessing office drew, or whether another source supported it. The next request should ask that office to disclose its reasoning. We will send the question with the old and corrected texts both visible.

court_docket_dated_application.speaker: narrator
court_docket_dated_application.text: The decision applying the verification cycle was dated after the emergency receipt. Its margin acknowledged the seven-day extension but still named the longer cycle for the unresolved annex. This order did not withdraw the protective receipt. It did mean that a reply about work scope might ordinarily wait far beyond the applicants' present needs. Shen Qing placed the orders in chronological sequence and copied their different subjects. The judge's signature appeared on the protective receipt; the classification clerk's initials appeared on the queue order. The two officials had made related decisions with different authority and different consequences.

court_docket_assessing_request.speaker: he_lian
court_docket_assessing_request.text: Ask the assessing office for the source of each disputed duty assignment and for the identity of the person who approved its reasoning. My morning receipt suspends this new assessment while that information is gathered. It does not certify the allegation that the assessment was fabricated, and it does not transfer the office's explanation into my own testimony. We will preserve the distinction even if the office responds badly. The seven-day review remains scheduled. Any proposed change to the longer verification process must identify what evidence it protects and which shorter steps can safely occur before it ends.

court_docket_questions_carried.speaker: narrator
court_docket_questions_carried.text: Tao Wen took the office question in a weatherproof cover with a delivery acknowledgment attached. He accepted a specified trip, not an open-ended duty to carry the entire inquiry. His own restored pay-account claim remained separate from this service. The court keeper recorded the sending time and the intended recipient, while Tao kept the route details in his own book. Lin Yue declined to copy the unrelated page beside them. A delivery receipt could later establish that the question reached a desk; it would not establish that its recipient had read or answered every sentence.

court_docket_city_claims.speaker: elder_yun
court_docket_city_claims.text: The city records still contain genuine commercial questions, and those should remain visible where they matter. We must not let the defective annex turn every license charge into false debt, just as we must not let an unresolved charge become ownership of a person's name. The landing injury is a new claim with its own evidence. It may require a different hearing even when the same people carry papers between offices. Keeping these matters distinct costs us a little more ink today. Combining them carelessly would cost somebody a second argument for a right already recognized.

court_docket_assessment_boundary.speaker: lin_yue
court_docket_assessment_boundary.text: I have written the suspended assessment in one box and physical safety restrictions in another. The receipt suspends the disputed civil charge and record-based work bar; it leaves restrictions on unsafe equipment intact. That means a valid worker may still be unable to use this sling while its condition is checked. It also means the office cannot use an uncertain filing to bar every unrelated job. We should ask how its notice communicated the difference. A person planning tomorrow's wages needs more than the general reassurance that the court has placed a mark beside their petition.

court_docket_reply_due.speaker: narrator
court_docket_reply_due.text: The keeper attached a reply slip to the office request, identifying the Day Seven review and the earlier Day Three shared hearing. The slip requested available source explanations for the earlier hearing, with any missing materials listed rather than invented. Luo Shan checked that it promised no automatic penalty for a late answer. A delayed response could affect what the court was able to conclude, but lateness alone would not establish the accident's cause. The office received a practical opportunity to answer and a clear account of the uncertainty its silence would leave.

court_docket_act_two_close.speaker: narrator
court_docket_act_two_close.text: At evening, the comparison sheet held four versions of the authority language and two distinct court orders. Luo Shan tied the source notes together without fastening them to the city judgment. The keeper returned the originals to their proper drawers and left the working packet on the dry shelf. Below the window, the corrected display card had acquired a second line explaining where a visitor could request help reading it. Tomorrow they would examine the seventy-five-day cycle itself: what it had been designed to verify, how it was adopted, and why the clock began only after a file became complete.

court_docket_day_one.speaker: narrator
court_docket_day_one.text: On Day One, the terrace smelled of wet cedar newly shaved for repairs. The keeper had placed a basin beneath the broken channel joint, leaving a covered lane for visitors who could walk it safely. Farther below, trained bearers prepared a carrying cradle on the covered footpath for Bai's reserved journey. The counterweighted goods lift remained closed. Lin Yue watched the bearers test their grips without treating the preparation as a promise that every journey would proceed. Staff checks and Bai's choice still governed the trip; a written account remained available if she declined it.

court_docket_calendar_volume.speaker: narrator
court_docket_calendar_volume.text: The standing calendar filled a broad bound volume. Its first pages described a court serving travelers whose papers arrived from several valleys, sometimes after months of interrupted roads. Seventy-five days allowed offices to search their retained records and answer contradictions before final verification. Later pages added procedures for urgent petitions. The current desk summary mentioned the long cycle prominently and the urgent procedures in smaller script. Shen Qing copied the adoption marks and amendment sequence. They needed to distinguish a legitimate waiting period for unavailable evidence from a habit of withholding every smaller decision until that period ended.

court_docket_old_need.speaker: he_lian
court_docket_old_need.text: The long search once prevented decisions based on a single ruined transport register. Offices had time to send their intact copies, and applicants could contest a mistaken match. Those protections still matter when a road fails. But they do not require us to pretend an admitted work proof is undecided, or that a simple source question must wait for all possible records. I have relied on the summary too readily. Before proposing a shorter procedure, identify which tasks truly need distant replies. A convenient new calendar would be another mistake if it discarded the evidence an absent person could supply.

court_docket_starting_clock.speaker: shen_qing
court_docket_starting_clock.text: The adopted rule begins its count when the docket certifies a complete verification packet. The front desk's receipt may be earlier. We have found files whose covers show only the later date because that was all the drawer label required. I am not adding those intervals together as proof of unlawful delay; some applicants asked for more time themselves. I am separating the stages so the interval can be explained. The landing packet has a known emergency receipt and a disputed completeness classification. Its protections run from the receipt, not from a later clerk's declaration that every document is present.

court_docket_permission_sample.speaker: narrator
court_docket_permission_sample.text: Luo Shan requested a small sample of completed files with their owners' permission, rather than opening an entire drawer for comparison. Two applicants agreed to provide dates, one supplied only a total interval, and another declined. The refused file remained closed. From the offered dates, the clerks could compare requested visits, material receipt, and final completeness. They could not infer the same pattern for everyone. Lin Yue left the declined file out of the tally and recorded the sampling limit. A modest set of willing examples might expose a procedural question without pretending to measure the whole court.

court_docket_apples_and_dates.speaker: narrator
court_docket_apples_and_dates.text: One offered file concerned a grower whose account lacked the buyer's reply. Its long interval included a delay the grower had requested while the buyer was abroad. Another concerned a repaired boundary marker, supported by a map held next door. Both had reached the same verification shelf. Luo Shan wrote their different missing items in large letters beneath the dates. The first example explained a genuine need for distant evidence; the second demanded an explanation of a local queue. A column of waiting days alone would have hidden the distinction as effectively as the single-date labels did.

court_docket_mortal_hours.speaker: luo_shan
court_docket_mortal_hours.text: A long-lived official can think of seventy-five days as a brief interval without intending harm. Deng has one kiln firing this month, and Du's shoulder will not wait for our convenience before affecting his wages. These are different kinds of time inside the same calendar. I would like each proposed verification step to name what it asks an applicant to do, how often, and by which date. That may reveal a needless appearance before we know anything about blame. It also leaves room for somebody who wants more time instead of being hurried for the sake of a tidy reform.

court_docket_clock_board.speaker: narrator
court_docket_clock_board.text: The wall board displayed the court's bell times, while the petition described the accident by the market's third bell. Luo Shan resisted aligning the columns by their matching numbers. The weather team was comparing current clocks and would report their limits separately. For scheduling, the office could state its own opening time and provide a plain daylight description. For reconstruction, that clarity would not retroactively synchronize the bells. Shen Qing wrote two separate notes. It was possible to improve tomorrow's invitation without claiming to know the exact moment of a jolt two days before their arrival.

court_docket_notice_reading.speaker: narrator
court_docket_notice_reading.text: Cai Fen read an old invitation aloud to a visitor who had difficulty with its dense script. It required attendance before the fourth ringing at the upper hall, without naming whose bell or describing the approach. The visitor assumed the market bell below. Cai described the court's bell and admitted that the invitation left the difference unstated. She offered to mark the next notice with the court's clock and a daylight interval. Lin Yue recorded the exchange with permission. A clearer invitation addressed a communication defect; it did not establish that the visitor's earlier arrival had been late.

court_docket_calendar_choice.speaker: lin_yue
court_docket_calendar_choice.text: There are three useful ways to test this calendar without declaring the entire rule worthless. We can compare the adoption minutes with later amendments, examine how the office describes a complete packet, or follow a corrected invitation through an applicant's practical schedule. Each will tell us something the other two cannot. The clerks handling the remaining inquiries will identify their own sources when they return. I want our eventual report to say which protection the long wait supplies and which smaller tasks could proceed meanwhile. A shorter number alone would not answer either question.

choices.text: Test an invitation against a shift

court_docket_minutes_path.speaker: narrator
court_docket_minutes_path.text: The adoption minutes preserved an argument between two judges. One feared that rapid decisions would silence a distant party; the other feared that repetitive appearances would exhaust an applicant before distant evidence arrived. Their agreement allowed local source checks during the long search and required reasons for withholding an interim reply. The desk summary had retained the search period and omitted the interim-reply instruction. Shen Qing copied the exchange without claiming either judge foresaw this particular landing case. The earlier disagreement offered a neglected tool, not an ancient endorsement of every change they might now propose.

court_docket_complete_path.speaker: narrator
court_docket_complete_path.text: The completeness checklist asked for a lawful work identifier, a description of the disputed event, and a means of contacting the opposing office. A handwritten extra line required a fully corroborated duty account. No adoption mark accompanied that addition. The classification clerk said she used it because uncertain duties frequently led to repeated requests. Luo Shan preserved the practical explanation alongside the missing authority. It showed a workflow problem the clerk had tried to solve. It did not show that she possessed power to make a complete liability account a condition for admitting a claim about that very liability.

court_docket_invitation_path.speaker: narrator
court_docket_invitation_path.text: A visitor planning an afternoon shift compared the old invitation with Cai's proposed wording. The daylight interval allowed him to estimate the covered walk, while an explicit option to submit a signed statement spared another journey if his shift changed. He asked who would acknowledge that statement so it could not disappear beneath the stair. Cai added the receiving desk's name and a request for a dated receipt. Lin Yue noted the visitor's suggestion and its limit. This was a test of understandable directions, not evidence that every worker could attend within the same interval.

court_docket_calendar_rejoin.speaker: luo_shan
court_docket_calendar_rejoin.text: The adopted minutes permit local checks and reasoned interim replies during the long search. The extra completeness line lacks an identified adoption mark. A corrected invitation can name its clock, receiving desk, and alternative submission route. Other clerks have supplied signed notes for the inquiries we did not follow. Together, these findings suggest immediate work already authorized by the standing rule, plus a question about the added requirement. They do not authorize us to abolish seventy-five days for distant contested records. We should ask the judge to distinguish existing powers from changes requiring formal notice and review.

court_docket_judge_distinction.speaker: he_lian
court_docket_judge_distinction.text: I can require a reasoned interim reply under the adopted minutes and examine the authority claimed for the extra checklist line. A durable replacement for the verification calendar is a different decision. It must address distant replies, absent parties, and applicants who need more time. The landing case's emergency receipt already protects it through the evidence extension review. We can prepare staged questions for this case without promising that all future cases will follow the same short schedule. Record that boundary in the draft. I will not let my signature on a present direction masquerade as an unannounced general rule.

court_docket_missing_signature.speaker: narrator
court_docket_missing_signature.text: The classification clerk brought the page from which she had copied the extra line. It came from an internal training example marked proposed practice, its lower edge torn before the page entered the desk folder. The retained master showed the complete heading. A senior clerk had used the example during instruction but denied authorizing it as a new admission condition. Luo Shan wrote both accounts beside their dated sources. The missing edge explained how the page might be misunderstood; it did not absolve every later officer who could have checked the master before relying on it.

court_docket_training_cost.speaker: elder_yun
court_docket_training_cost.text: A proposed practice can become an obligation through repetition without anyone signing that obligation openly. We should ask who had responsibility for checking the training folder and what opportunity the classification clerk had to consult the master. The answer may distribute responsibility rather than place it all in one hand. It also tells us what repair will last: a new heading, supervision, time to read the source, or some combination. If we demand careful checking while keeping the same impossible queue, the next shortened page may acquire the same authority for the same practical reason.

court_docket_applicant_reply.speaker: narrator
court_docket_applicant_reply.text: Bai's funded visit reached the sheltered receiving area after the bearers completed their safety checks. Luo Shan asked only about her notice and filing choices, leaving the witness team to examine her equipment account. Bai could give a written reply to the duty questions before Day Three. She could not promise to return for every copied annex that appeared. They wrote that preference beside her contact route, with her approval. The carrying cradle waited on the covered footpath for her return, separate from the closed goods lift whose condition remained part of the dispute.

court_docket_days_named.speaker: lin_yue
court_docket_days_named.text: I have put the Day Three shared hearing, Day Five possible canal closure, and Day Seven extension review on separate lines. The closure is a forecast, so our transport plan should prepare for it without treating it as a fact already happened. Day Seven is a review date, not a promise that every liability question will be settled then. The longer verification cycle concerns unresolved evidence, while the emergency receipt gives present protection. Naming each purpose prevents one date from swallowing the others. Bai should be able to plan her reply from this page without guessing which deadline we mean.

court_docket_evening_rule.speaker: narrator
court_docket_evening_rule.text: Before the desk closed, He Lian issued a direction requiring the classification office to state its reasons for the added completeness line and identify the source of that authority. The direction cited the existing interim-reply provision. It did not repeal the standing calendar or certify the accident account. Cai posted a plain explanation for visitors asking about new invitations, while the keeper retained the superseded wording in a cover. The ordinary clerks performed this work within their funded shifts. Luo Shan marked the task as existing administration, avoiding a second charge against the finite access fund.

court_docket_act_three_close.speaker: narrator
court_docket_act_three_close.text: Their calendar sheet now showed several clocks rather than one long blank wait. A protected claimant could receive a local source explanation before distant verification ended; a proposed checklist did not become an adopted rule simply because its torn copy lived on the desk. Those findings still left the substance of the duty assignment unresolved. As Bai returned safely down the covered path, Lin Yue opened the work-scope file. The next question was harder than making a notice readable: which person had actually undertaken each landing task, and how the court's annex had expanded that account.

court_docket_scope_bundle.speaker: narrator
court_docket_scope_bundle.text: The work-scope bundle was tied with a darker cord than the accident papers. Bai had offered the relevant portion of her daily contract, while the lift office supplied its equipment-duty page under the court's source request. Each keeper retained the original. Luo Shan unfolded ordinary working copies and wrote their status across the top before anyone compared the words. One described landing and guide inspection. The other assigned counterweight and brake maintenance to separate lift staff. Their overlap at the lower landing did not merge the jobs, although the annex's broad heading made that merger appear almost natural.

court_docket_bai_scope.speaker: luo_shan
court_docket_bai_scope.text: Bai's undertaking concerns the landing surface, guide path, and daily inspection within that stated remit. The contract is a source for assigned work, not proof that she fulfilled every part of it on the accident day. Likewise, the equipment page assigns other staff the counterweight and brake tasks without proving those tasks were done. We need both distinctions. If we call the contract a complete defense, we would decide conduct from a heading. If we ignore it, we could charge Bai for work she never accepted. The actual inspections and the disputed sequence still require their own evidence.

court_docket_lift_office.speaker: narrator
court_docket_lift_office.text: The lift office's reply arrived before sunset on Day One. It described the counterweighted sling as ordinary goods equipment and identified separate maintenance roles. Its foreman, Yan Chao, forty-seven, disputed the petition's implication that every sling fault lay outside the guide worker's possible responsibility. A bad guide condition might contribute even when the brake had its own keeper, he wrote. Luo Shan copied the reply without treating that hypothetical as an observation of this accident. The office had raised a plausible category of contribution. It had not supplied evidence showing that contribution occurred.

court_docket_contract_margin.speaker: shen_qing
court_docket_contract_margin.text: A later margin adds report visible obstruction promptly. The keeper identifies it as an acknowledged amendment to Bai's contract, with her signature beside the date. That language creates a reporting duty within her ordinary view; it does not assign concealed brake repair or inspection inside the counterweight housing. We should preserve the amendment because omitting it would make the offered contract incomplete. Bai can explain what she understood and observed. The report can then distinguish an assigned duty, a claimed action, and a disputed condition. Each needs a different kind of answer from the court.

court_docket_authority_grid.speaker: narrator
court_docket_authority_grid.text: They ruled a fresh sheet into four columns: assigned task, offered account of performance, physical condition, and disputed consequence. The court annex had compressed all four into responsibility confirmed. Lin Yue copied that phrase in a separate margin, retaining its source. Bai's morning walk belonged under offered account until the witness team reported it. A maintenance signature belonged under claimed performance, with its author identified. The injury belonged under consequence but did not identify its cause. The grid made the disagreement longer on paper and narrower in meaning, which was a better bargain than a short accusation.

court_docket_licensing_limit.speaker: lin_yue
court_docket_licensing_limit.text: A work proof tells the office which living worker stands behind a claim. A temporary recognition-use license describes a permitted public persona. Neither identifies who maintained a concealed brake or whether a safety rope was up before a particular descent. The annex used the license heading as if it answered those questions. I am marking that as an unsupported step until its author supplies another source. We can recognize lawful work and still investigate a worker's conduct. We can also question conduct without returning to the old practice of treating a commercial paper as ownership of a person's public name.

court_docket_maintenance_entry.speaker: narrator
court_docket_maintenance_entry.text: An ordinary clerk brought the offered maintenance entry in a sealed viewing folder. Its signature indicated that scheduled brake work had been recorded on the relevant morning. The entry did not describe the guide surface, and its time referred to the office's own bell. Luo Shan asked whether the signer personally performed the work or recorded another worker's report. The clerk could not answer from the page alone. They copied the entry's wording and requested the signer's explanation. A signature gave the inquiry an accountable source; it did not remove the need to learn what that source actually knew.

court_docket_source_roles.speaker: he_lian
court_docket_source_roles.text: The duty pages may narrow a claim, but they cannot settle the sequence by themselves. Ask the office to identify who assigned the tasks, who performed the recorded inspection, and who entered the note. Those may be three people. The court should not reward a tidy form by treating its initials as all three. Nor should an uncertain signature make the entire maintenance account worthless. We will give its author an opportunity to explain the record and answer the petition. The provisional protections continue while these questions are put. The closed equipment remains closed for safety.

court_docket_physical_boundary.speaker: narrator
court_docket_physical_boundary.text: From the terrace, Lin Yue could see the goods lift's upper wheel but not the lower guide joint. The distance tempted a quick diagram with invented detail. Instead, she drew only what the terrace showed and marked the unseen area with a shaded rectangle. The weather packet carries inspection staff's permitted notes. A separate rope closed the approach to the lift; the covered footpath remained available under staff checks. The two routes shared part of the cliff but served different purposes. Showing them separately prevented an argument about hearing access from becoming an argument for reopening unsafe goods equipment.

court_docket_duty_choice.speaker: lin_yue
court_docket_duty_choice.text: We can test the annex's broad responsibility heading against the original duty pages, the recorded inspection's authorship, or the physical limits of each worker's ordinary view. The other teams will preserve their answers for comparison. I want our report to identify exactly where the heading exceeds its source, while leaving actual performance and cause open. It would be easy to replace one broad claim with its opposite and call that fairness. The harder task is to keep Bai's accepted duties visible, the lift staff's duties visible, and each disputed observation attached to the person able to answer for it.

court_docket_duties_path.speaker: narrator
court_docket_duties_path.text: After descending, Bai read the offered contract passages with the lower contact and indicated the reporting amendment. Her approved reply accepted responsibility for visible guide obstructions and the ordinary landing walk. It did not claim exemption from every possible contribution to an accident. She asked the assessing office to identify the neglected act it alleged. Luo Shan received the checked reply, preserving its contact route and readback. The original stayed with its keeper. Her clarification supplied no admission that she had seen an obstruction or failed to report one, and required no second ascent.

court_docket_signer_path.speaker: narrator
court_docket_signer_path.text: Yan Chao identified the maintenance signer as the worker who recorded his own brake check. He could confirm assigning that check, but he had not stood beside the worker throughout it. His earlier statement that the equipment was checked came from the completed entry. The worker had been sent the court's source questions and had not yet supplied an answer. Shen Qing preserved the foreman's confirmation of assignment and his limit on performance. The office now had two related sources, not two independent observations of the brake's condition at the moment the sling slipped.

court_docket_view_path.speaker: narrator
court_docket_view_path.text: An equipment clerk described the normal guide walk using an unoccupied demonstration route on the terrace. From one position, a worker could inspect the landing edge but not the brake housing below the wheel cover. From another, the housing opened only after an authorized keeper removed its fastening. Lin Yue recorded the demonstrated access limits. She did not enter the closed lift or claim the demonstration reproduced the accident's exact arrangement. The explanation helped interpret the contract's ordinary-view duty. It left open what each person saw that morning and whether an abnormal condition changed the usual view.

court_docket_duty_rejoin.speaker: luo_shan
court_docket_duty_rejoin.text: The original pages assign landing and guide inspection to Bai and counterweight and brake maintenance to separate lift staff. Bai also accepts reporting visible obstructions within that remit. The maintenance entry records a check whose signer still owes an explanation; the foreman confirms assignment without witnessing the whole performance. The view demonstration supplies a limit, not an accident reconstruction. These findings come from our direct work and the other teams' signed notes. They justify separating the annex's broad heading into specific questions. They establish neither that Bai fulfilled every duty nor that the brake keeper caused Du's injury.

court_docket_assessment_language.speaker: narrator
court_docket_assessment_language.text: The assessing office sent a brief reply describing its broad heading as an administrative convenience. It had grouped connected landing tasks while deciding which records to request. Luo Shan asked why that grouping then appeared in a civil assessment addressed to a particular worker. The office had not answered that second question. He Lian directed the keeper to preserve both the explanation and the unanswered passage. An internal grouping might help an office gather papers. Once used to assign a charge, its imprecision acquired consequences that could not be excused merely by repeating the original convenience.

court_docket_bai_disagreement.speaker: lin_yue
court_docket_bai_disagreement.text: Bai wants the whole assessment withdrawn because its duty heading is too broad. The office wants the heading retained until it gathers every source. We need to show both positions without pretending either follows automatically from our comparison. A defective basis can require a corrected explanation or reconsideration while leaving a properly supported claim possible. The emergency receipt already prevents this disputed assessment from imposing its current charge or work bar. At the shared hearing, the court will choose a bounded way forward. This branch should give that choice accurate questions, including the parts each side has not answered.

court_docket_separate_damage.speaker: narrator
court_docket_separate_damage.text: Du's claim included pain, interrupted wages, and the need for ordinary care. The access fund paid none of those damages. Luo Shan copied the claim headings without inserting a sum where the petition left one open. The relevant wage and verification annex would be available in a baseline certified working extract, while other comparisons remained ordinary clerk notes. They had no authority to turn the fund's unspent portion into compensation. A hearing made reachable could still fail to resolve a serious material loss. That fact belonged in the report beside the procedural repairs rather than beneath a reassuring conclusion.

court_docket_maintenance_questions.speaker: shen_qing
court_docket_maintenance_questions.text: Our next source request asks what the recorded brake check included, which clock supplied its time, and whether a later change was entered separately. It also asks the guide office to identify any specific obstruction it alleges Bai should have reported. We are not asking either office to endorse a complete accident story before its evidence is heard. Each can supply a narrow answer and state what remains unknown. I have put the closed-equipment condition in the margin so the request cannot be read as permission to perform a demonstration with Du's ordinary goods sling.

court_docket_reserved_extract.speaker: narrator
court_docket_reserved_extract.text: The keeper confirmed that the two funded certified working extracts covered the offered incident and maintenance entries, and the offered wage and verification annex entries. Their original keepers would retain the source books. No additional certification was ordered for the team's comparison grid or the already supplied city packet. Luo Shan marked those as ordinary working notes so their usefulness would not inflate the access budget. The distinction also mattered for authority: a clerk's signed comparison could explain a method, but its conclusions remained open to challenge even when a certified source extract lay beside it.

court_docket_quiet_dispute.speaker: elder_yun
court_docket_quiet_dispute.text: It is possible for Bai to be wrong about some act she performed and right that this assessment assigns her too much. It is possible for the lift office to have a sound maintenance record and an unsound explanation of its wider consequences. We should keep that possibility alive without using it as an excuse to avoid findings we can make. The scope pages are clear enough to identify separate duties. The actual event remains contested. A careful court can state the first plainly while refusing to manufacture certainty about the second. That refusal should carry a practical next step.

court_docket_act_four_close.speaker: narrator
court_docket_act_four_close.text: By the end of Day One, the grid contained named tasks instead of an undivided category of landing responsibility. The office's convenience explanation remained unanswered where it became a particular assessment. Bai's return journey had finished on the covered footpath, and the goods lift had not moved. Luo Shan placed the source requests in their sending order. Tomorrow's replies might narrow conduct or reveal another copying error. Before any of them entered the shared packet, the team would examine who could handle the offered records and how a correction could travel without making its earlier version disappear.

court_docket_day_two_shelf.speaker: narrator
court_docket_day_two_shelf.text: On Day Two, the keeper found a viewing cover tucked beneath the blotting board. It held an ordinary copy of the maintenance question, not the source entry. Its absence had nevertheless left the sending register looking incomplete. Luo Shan returned it to the correct cover and noted where it had been found, without describing the misplacement as theft. The original source books remained with their keepers. Lin Yue asked how the office distinguished a missing copy from a missing exhibit. In a crowded room, the difference needed to be visible before somebody built an accusation around an empty slot.

court_docket_cover_marks.speaker: shen_qing
court_docket_cover_marks.text: These covers use the same color for originals, certified extracts, and working notes. Their written labels are accurate, but a hurried clerk can miss them. We can propose distinct corner marks while keeping the present labels and dates. That is an aid to handling, not a new rank of truth. An original statement can be mistaken, a certified extract can reproduce a mistaken entry faithfully, and an ordinary note can contain a useful question. The marks should tell a keeper what custody is required and what source to consult, without pretending the colored cover decides what happened.

court_docket_offered_limits.speaker: narrator
court_docket_offered_limits.text: The keepers' permission sheets allowed relevant entries to be viewed and the two funded extracts to be made. Other pages stayed covered, including private wage arrangements unrelated to the accident. Luo Shan added a removable guard sheet rather than cutting a page or blackening the book. Each viewer signed for the offered portion and returned it before another took the table. The sequence was slower than handing the whole book around. It also left the keeper able to show what had been seen, which matters a great deal when somebody later claims a hidden page confirmed their account.

court_docket_public_and_private.speaker: lin_yue
court_docket_public_and_private.text: A public correction of work proof and a private account of injury do not need the same circulation. We can cite the admitted city judgment where required while keeping Du's unrelated household costs outside the shared packet. The permission for an offered wage entry covers that entry, not every person paid on the page beside it. I want our source list to name what may be shown at the hearing and what may only be checked with its keeper. If a disputed fact needs a further portion, we must ask rather than let curiosity enlarge the original offer.

court_docket_witness_correction.speaker: narrator
court_docket_witness_correction.text: The witness team supplied Du's original brief report alongside a dated correction. Its earlier phrase said the safety rope was absent. The correction narrowed that to his own observation: he had not seen a rope before the jolt and saw one after the injury. He could not date its first installation. Luo Shan preserved both versions, the reason for the correction, and Du's approval. The change did not automatically destroy his account or turn the original sentence into proof. It gave the court a clearer limit on what the injured porter could personally establish about the disputed sequence.

court_docket_correction_reason.speaker: luo_shan
court_docket_correction_reason.text: A witness may discover that the first summary states more than the witness actually knew. We should welcome a correction while preserving enough history for another party to question it. Du's account of the jolt remains his offered recollection. His rope statement now distinguishes not seeing something from knowing it was absent. We can carry both versions with the team's explanation, without presenting them as two witnesses agreeing or disagreeing. The same principle applies to our annex. If its author changes a scope claim, the earlier wording should remain visible so the court can examine who relied on it.

court_docket_independent_accounts.speaker: narrator
court_docket_independent_accounts.text: Another source note identified Su E, a fifty-year-old baker, who heard the market's third bell near the lower gate. Chen Yuan, a fifty-two-year-old potter, described people carrying a coil after a shout. The witness team kept these accounts separate from Du's, with each person's permission and stated vantage. Su E did not synchronize the court's bell. Chen did not see the earlier lift configuration. Luo Shan put each narrow observation on its own line. Repeating their names in an attendance summary would not create further testimony, and combining their limits would not produce a complete view no one possessed.

court_docket_weather_permission.speaker: rain_heron
court_docket_weather_permission.text: I offered what I saw from my permitted perches and what my own log records. You may carry the agreed passages with the locations named correctly. A keeper once described the inner rail as the outer terrace in a copy; that error changes what a reader imagines I could see. Preserve the correction beside the first description. I will not make an unsafe outer flight to give your file a more impressive ending. My refusal adds no observation about the old accident. If you need another record, ask its keeper. My wings are not the court's missing page.

court_docket_weather_source.speaker: narrator
court_docket_weather_source.text: The weather team's note described present gauge undercollection in controlled pours and current disagreement between clocks. Neither observation reconstructed the exact rain or bell offset on the accident day. A dated slate placed gauge-support replacement on the following day, separately from sling equipment work. The Heron's two offered inner-rail log extracts remained one witness; a revised bulletin supplied no mechanical observation. Lin Yue copied these limits before the attractive details. A present tilted gauge could explain why another measurement deserved caution; it could not fill every blank in a retrospective account.

court_docket_custody_choice.speaker: lin_yue
court_docket_custody_choice.text: We can now test whether the packet carries these limits intact. One route follows a correction from its author to the file, another checks permission and custody at the source books, and a third rehearses how a reader might mistake copied summaries for independent testimony. Clerks will report the routes we do not watch. I want the packet to be usable, not merely careful in this room. A qualification that falls away during copying is almost as absent as one never written. The test should show where a reader can find the retained source and the reason for a change.

court_docket_correction_path.speaker: narrator
court_docket_correction_path.text: A clerk received a practice correction attached to its first version, then entered the change in the amendment column. She initially filed only the corrected sheet in the viewing cover because the cover's label asked for current text. Luo Shan pointed to the retained-history instruction, and she added a source reference to the earlier version's storage cover. They repeated the handoff until both could be located from the viewing label. The rehearsal used invented practice content marked as such, never an accident statement. It exposed a handling weakness without altering a witness's actual testimony to test the system.

court_docket_keepers_path.speaker: narrator
court_docket_keepers_path.text: The incident-book keeper watched Shen Qing request the agreed entry and its adjoining date heading. When the request reached beyond the offered portion, the keeper stopped the page turn and asked what additional fact was needed. Shen explained the missing heading and sought a narrow extension of permission. The keeper agreed to that heading alone, leaving unrelated names covered. They wrote the extension beside the original permission. Lin Yue's source note described the exchange, not the hidden names. The check showed that a viewer could identify a real gap without treating an initial offer as unlimited access.

court_docket_reader_path.speaker: narrator
court_docket_reader_path.text: The keeper gave Cai Fen a sample packet containing a statement, a copied attendance summary, and an index citing both. She first counted three records and then asked whether they contained three sources. The sample's arrows led back to one statement. Luo Shan added a source-line field to the demonstration cover and asked her to read it again. This time she separated record count from witness count immediately. The demonstration could not prove every clerk would do the same under pressure. It showed a specific improvement worth testing with the real packet while its distinct sources remained visible.

court_docket_custody_rejoin.speaker: shen_qing
court_docket_custody_rejoin.text: The correction handoff needs a visible route to retained history. A permission can be extended for a named missing heading without opening unrelated entries. A source-line field helps distinguish copied records from independent observations. We have notes for the checks other clerks performed. These are handling findings, not testimony about the sling. I have applied the agreed labels to our working packet while leaving original books with their keepers. The two certified extracts retain their source references; ordinary comparison sheets retain theirs. A reader at the shared hearing can trace any claim without accepting our cover color as proof.

court_docket_du_visit.speaker: narrator
court_docket_du_visit.text: Du's funded Day Two round trip brought him along the covered footpath after the staff and medical checks. The attendants guarded his injured right shoulder while helping him from the carrying cradle. He confirmed the offered correction and the portions of his wage account the hearing could use. He declined to discuss unrelated household debts in the corridor. Luo Shan marked that refusal without treating it as a flaw in the accident claim. The closed goods lift remained unused. Later hearing access would rely on his authorized records rather than requiring another journey the baseline fund had not promised.

court_docket_physical_handling.speaker: lin_yue
court_docket_physical_handling.text: The original papers have owners and keepers even when their contents matter to a public dispute. Our court packet can be complete enough for a bounded hearing without becoming the warehouse for every source book. Let us list where each original will remain and who can answer a challenged transcription. That also protects an absent respondent. If a comparison sheet misquotes the maintenance entry, the respondent needs a way to point to the offered original rather than fight our handwriting from memory. We should build that route before the argument, while the keeper can still check the reference calmly.

court_docket_storage_term.speaker: narrator
court_docket_storage_term.text: The keeper set aside the funded storage space for six nights, beginning with arrival night and ending after Night Five. The scheduled collection was the morning of Day Six. Luo Shan copied those dates beside the source-location list, leaving no vague promise of indefinite storage. The ordinary court drawers retained their own records under existing rules; the paid space concerned the offered materials requiring temporary protection. A later extension would need an actual arrangement and funds, not merely another signature on the cover. The possible Day Five canal closure made a timely collection plan prudent, without making the forecast certain.

court_docket_challenged_copy.speaker: narrator
court_docket_challenged_copy.text: Yan Chao sent a note disputing one working transcription of his earlier reply. The phrase might contribute had become did contribute when copied into a clerk's private summary. Shen Qing compared the signed reply, acknowledged the error, and corrected the summary with the first wording retained. No assessment source used that private summary yet. Luo Shan recorded the error because leaving it invisible would invite the same mistake later. The correction restored a hypothetical to its proper status. It did not prove the foreman's hypothesis true, and it did not justify calling his whole reply unreliable.

court_docket_our_responsibility.speaker: shen_qing
court_docket_our_responsibility.text: This mistake came from our side of the table. I have corrected it and identified the source, but the method still needs a check before the shared hearing. One clerk can read each disputed sentence while another points to the offered passage. We should reserve that effort for statements whose wording affects scope or sequence, rather than exhaust the staff by pretending every repeated courtesy needs two readers. Ordinary clerk time is already funded; it is finite even so. I will put the priority list on the cover so the next shift knows why these particular lines require attention.

court_docket_bounded_sources.speaker: elder_yun
court_docket_bounded_sources.text: An orderly packet can make us forget that it contains offers, recollections, and disputed conclusions rather than a finished event. The source routes preserve a way to question our work. The permissions preserve a way to say no to a different use. Neither is a decorative assurance. When someone at the hearing wants a broader page, another flight, or a further journey, the court must ask what that request would add and who can actually authorize it. A witness's earlier cooperation should never be treated as the answer to every request that becomes convenient after the argument begins.

court_docket_act_five_close.speaker: narrator
court_docket_act_five_close.text: The packet now had source routes, dated corrections, and separate permissions instead of a single seal claiming completeness. Du's return cradle left by the covered path, and the keeper checked the storage list against the funded term. Lin Yue watched the clerk release the intake trickle and enter its paired receipt. That desk signal explained nothing about the paper's earlier journey.
